repository.name: kicad-mcp-pro
repository.readme:
KiCad MCP Pro

Drive KiCad schematic, PCB, DRC/ERC, DFM, and manufacturing review from any MCP-capable AI agent.

Documentation · Installation · Quick Start · Tool Reference · AI Agent Setup · AI discovery

[![KiCad programmatic parity](https://img.shields.io/badge/KiCad_programmatic_parity-85.7%25-green)](docs/compatibility/capability-parity.generated.md)

KiCad MCP Pro is a Model Context Protocol server for KiCad EDA workflows. It exposes tools, resources, and prompts for schematic, PCB, validation, DFM, and manufacturing export automation. The server now starts with the bounded `default` profile: 24 read-only review tools instead of the complete expert catalog. Use `build` with write mode for controlled edits, `release` with manufacturing mode for human-gated handoff, or `expert`/`full` only for advanced trusted clients. Current catalog counts and context-size estimates come from [`docs/evidence/progressive-disclosure-profile-snapshot.json`](docs/evidence/progressive-disclosure-profile-snapshot.json); see [`docs/agents/progressive-disclosure.md`](docs/agents/progressive-disclosure.md). Telemetry and error reporting are disabled by default. Opt-in OpenTelemetry configuration is documented in [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md#opentelemetry), and privacy rules are documented in [`docs/privacy.md`](docs/privacy.md). ## Scope and honesty KiCad MCP Pro is a **professional first-pass design and review assistant**, not an automated sign-off authority. ERC/DRC and the export pipeline drive KiCad's own engines. The signal-integrity, power-integrity, EMC, and thermal tools are **first-order, closed-form estimates** (typically ~5–10% accuracy) — fast first-pass review, **not** a substitute for a 2D/3D field solver, EM/FEA simulation, or formal sign-off. Live component sourcing uses the JLCPCB public catalog by default; Nexar, DigiKey, and Mouser are available only when their API credentials are configured. What fraction of KiCad's programmatic surface the server drives is tracked openly in the [capability-parity matrix](docs/compatibility/capability-parity.generated.md). Raw tool count and capability coverage are inventory metrics, not the headline product-quality measure. End-to-end task outcome, mutation recovery, corruption, required DRC execution, and manufacturing reproducibility are the outcome KPIs. The committed [native-live example evidence](docs/evidence/task-outcomes/2026-08-28-native-live-example/) intentionally reports `insufficient_evidence`; representative-corpus target attainment remains separate until the qualification work in #730 is complete. ## Project identity | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Canonical repository | [`oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro`](https://github.com/oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro) | | PyPI package | [`kicad-mcp-pro`](https://pypi.org/project/kicad-mcp-pro/) | | npm wrapper | [`kicad-mcp-pro`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/kicad-mcp-pro) | | MCP Registry name | `io.github.oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro` | | Version | `4.5.0` | | OSS maturity report | [`docs/repo-maturity-report.md`](docs/repo-maturity-report.md) | | OpenSSF evidence | [`docs/openssf-evidence.md`](docs/openssf-evidence.md) | ## Quick Start ### Desktop App Download the latest installer from the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro/releases). The Tauri desktop app starts the Python dashboard server automatically and opens the GUI at `http://127.0.0.1:3334/ui`. Desktop releases launch the matching exact backend version and verify its desktop compatibility handshake before use; see [Installation](docs/installation.md#desktopbackend-compatibility). ### CLI ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro init uvx kicad-mcp-pro tray uvx kicad-mcp-pro dashboard --open uvx kicad-mcp-pro --transport streamable-http --port 3334 ``` ### KiCad PCB Editor Companion (development preview) The existing KiCad PCM Companion is being upgraded to a KiCad 10 IPC toolbar plugin in [packages/kicad-plugin/](packages/kicad-plugin/). It reads the active PCB and links to the existing local dashboard. The IPC upgrade is read-only; live desktop acceptance and release are pending. ### Web Dashboard ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3334 --open # http://127.0.0.1:3334/ui ``` ## Documentation The documentation is organized from setup to operation: 1. [Installation](docs/installation.md) 2. [Client configuration](docs/client-configuration.md) 3. [Runtime configuration](docs/configuration.md) 4. [Tool reference](docs/tools-reference.md) 5. [Workflows](docs/workflows/first-pcb.md) 6. [Release process](docs/release-process.md) 7. [Security and privacy](docs/security/threat-model.md) 8. [KiCad capability parity](docs/compatibility/capability-parity.generated.md) — how much of KiCad's programmatic surface this server drives 9. [Error code catalog](docs/errors.md) — stable error codes, retry classes, and recovery 10. [Work-order audit](docs/status/work-order-audit-2026-06-17.md) — current status of the hardening work order The `kicad_capability_parity()` tool reports, per workflow domain, what fraction of KiCad's programmatically reachable surface this server can drive (currently **76.6%**), keeping genuine `gap`s distinct from `gui-only-no-api` items that KiCad exposes no headless API for. The published documentation site is available at [https://oaslananka.github.io/kicad-mcp-pro/](https://oaslananka.github.io/kicad-mcp-pro/). ## Transports KiCad MCP Pro supports `stdio` and Streamable HTTP. Streamable HTTP is served at `/mcp` by default and can be moved with `KICAD_MCP_MOUNT_PATH`. ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro --transport streamable-http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3334 ``` Streamable HTTP clients must send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` and `Content-Type: application/json`. The primary public MCP contract is `2026-07-28`: modern clients send `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28`, the method/name transport headers required by the final protocol, and the per-request client metadata envelope. Backward-compatible `2025-11-25` clients remain supported through the SDK's legacy `initialize` negotiation. Those clients echo the negotiated protocol version on follow-up requests and, when `KICAD_MCP_STATEFUL_HTTP=1`, also echo `MCP-Session-Id`. Final `2026-07-28` traffic is stateless and does not create MCP sessions. The deprecated HTTP+SSE fallback routes are disabled by default. Set `KICAD_MCP_LEGACY_SSE=1` only for older clients that cannot use Streamable HTTP. ## Install Published packages: ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro --help npx kicad-mcp-pro --help ``` Fresh source checkout on supported Linux hosts: ```bash ./scripts/bootstrap-dev.sh source .dev-env.sh pnpm run dev:doctor -- --ci ``` The repository bootstrap installs checksum-pinned Python, uv/uvx, Node.js, pnpm, Task, and Rust tooling into ignored checkout-local roots and performs frozen dependency installation. It does not modify global tool directories. See the [reproducible bootstrap guide](docs/development/reproducible-bootstrap.md) for `--core-only`, `--check`, cleanup, upgrade, and KiCad capability modes. ## Package metadata The canonical metadata inputs are `pyproject.toml` for package version and repository identity, and `compatibility.yaml` for KiCad and MCP support policy. `server.json` is the generated registry manifest. `pnpm run metadata:sync` renders the public surfaces, and `pnpm run metadata:check` verifies them in CI and release validation. ## Usage Use `kicad-mcp-pro --help` to inspect CLI commands and [`docs/client-configuration.md`](docs/client-configuration.md) to configure an MCP client. The generated tool catalog is available in [`docs/tools-reference.generated.md`](docs/tools-reference.generated.md). ## Agent plugin and skills This repository owns the product-level agent plugin and KiCad-specific skills for KiCad MCP Pro. The central [`agent-tools`](https://github.com/oaslananka/agent-tools) repository should catalog this plugin, but the manifest and workflow instructions live here so they stay synchronized with the actual MCP server tools. | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | [`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`](.claude-plugin/plugin.json) | Product-level plugin manifest for compatible agent runtimes and marketplace catalogs. | | [`.mcp.json`](.mcp.json) | Claude Code project-local MCP server configuration. | | [`.codex/config.example.toml`](.codex/config.example.toml) | Codex CLI MCP configuration example. | | [`.vscode/mcp.example.json`](.vscode/mcp.example.json) | VS Code / GitHub Copilot workspace MCP configuration example. | | [`integrations/opencode/opencode.example.json`](integrations/opencode/opencode.example.json) | OpenCode project MCP configuration example. | | [`.opencode/skills/`](.opencode/skills) | OpenCode-native mirrored skill definitions. | | [`docs/agent-runtime-config.md`](docs/agent-runtime-config.md) | Agent runtime setup and validation matrix. | | [`skills/kicad-design-review/SKILL.md`](skills/kicad-design-review/SKILL.md) | Comprehensive KiCad design review skill. | | [`skills/pcb-design/SKILL.md`](skills/pcb-design/SKILL.md) | PCB design, layout inspection, placement, routing, stackup, and board-quality workflow. | | [`skills/drc-check/SKILL.md`](skills/drc-check/SKILL.md) | ERC/DRC execution, triage, waiver review, and revalidation workflow. | | [`skills/fabrication-output/SKILL.md`](skills/fabrication-output/SKILL.md) | Manufacturing export, DFM, release evidence, and fabrication-package workflow. | | [`skills/schematic-review/SKILL.md`](skills/schematic-review/SKILL.md) | Schematic inspection, ERC, connectivity, power, symbol, and readability workflow. | ### Agent setup KiCad MCP Pro can be launched with the published Python package, npm wrapper, or the container metadata declared in [`server.json`](server.json). Common local starts are: ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro --transport stdio uvx kicad-mcp-pro --transport streamable-http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3334 npx kicad-mcp-pro --help ``` For source checkouts, run the normal repository validation path before publishing plugin changes: ```bash corepack pnpm run metadata:check python3 -m json.tool .claude-plugin/plugin.json >/dev/null ``` ### Validation workflow Before listing this plugin as active from `agent-tools`, verify at least one compatible agent runtime can: 1. Discover `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. 2. Launch or connect to `kicad-mcp-pro` over `stdio` or Streamable HTTP. 3. Call `kicad_get_server_info` or `kicad_get_project_info`. 4. Load a skill from `skills/` and follow the workflow without referencing missing tools. 5. Report ERC, DRC, DFM, export artifacts, assumptions, and human-review requirements separately. KiCad MCP Pro is an engineering assistant, not an autonomous manufacturing sign-off authority. Generated PCB and fabrication outputs require qualified human review before fabrication or assembly. ## Development New contributors should start with [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md), which maps the five layers (transport → MCP protocol → orchestration → KiCad adapter seam → pure domain) and shows exactly how to add a new tool. The runtime model and quality-gate stack are documented in [`docs/development/architecture.md`](docs/development/architecture.md). The project uses a `Taskfile.yml` for common development commands. After cloning the repository: ```bash task install # Install all dependencies (pnpm + uv) task verify # Run the local quality gate: lint → format → typecheck → test → build task test # Run unit tests only task lint # Run lint and metadata checks task format # Auto-format the codebase task typecheck # Run strict static type checking task build # Build release artifacts task ci # Run the local equivalent of the full CI pipeline task hooks # Install repository-pinned Lefthook git hooks ``` All changes must pass `task verify` before opening a pull request. ## Contributing Read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. All changes must pass the repository's format, lint, type-check, test, workflow, security, and package metadata gates. ## Independent industry coverage - **JLCPCB (October 14, 2026)** — [KiCad MCP: How to Design a PCB with Claude Code](https://jlcpcb.com/blog/kicad-mcp-how-to-design-a-pcb-with-claude-code) documents a hands-on KiCad MCP Pro workflow for an XL4015/LM358 buck-converter design, including checks and limitations. The board was not fabricated or bench-tested. This is independent coverage, not a JLCPCB endorsement or partnership; reported issues are being evaluated in [#1314](https://github.com/oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro/issues/1314). ## Cite this software If you use KiCad MCP Pro in research or a technical publication, cite the archived release via its DOI (see [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff) for full metadata): ```bibtex @software{aslan_kicad_mcp_pro, author = {Aslan, Osman}, title = {KiCad MCP Pro}, license = {MIT}, url = {https://github.com/oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro}, doi = {10.5281/zenodo.21283791} } ``` Every GitHub release is archived on Zenodo under this concept DOI, which always resolves to the most recent version. ## License KiCad MCP Pro is available under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

# Protect post-merge evidence: each main commit retains its own CI run.
# On PRs, only the newest test run for that PR should consume runners.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' }}

jobs:
  changes:
    if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      docs: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      docs_only: ${{ steps.check.outputs.docs_only }}
      release_metadata_only: ${{ steps.release-classifier.outputs.release_metadata_only }}
      sonar_docs_only: ${{ steps.sonar-docs.outputs.docs_only }}
      python: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.python }}
      repo_tooling: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.repo_tooling }}
      npm: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.npm }}
      chatgpt_app: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.chatgpt_app }}
      schemas: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.schemas }}
      workflows: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.workflows }}
      dependencies: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.dependencies }}
      rustsec: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.rustsec }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            python:
              - 'src/**'
              - 'tests/**'
              - 'pyproject.toml'
              - 'uv.lock'
              - 'uv.toml'
              - 'scripts/**'
              - 'conftest.py'
              - 'pyrightconfig.json'
              - '.python-version'
              - 'performance/**'
              - 'evals/**'
            repo_tooling:
              - 'package.json'
              - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
              - 'Dockerfile'
              - 'docker-compose.yml'
              - 'lefthook.yml'
              - '.pre-commit-config.yaml'
              - 'Taskfile.yml'
              - '.mergify.yml'
              - '.github/dependabot.yml'
              - '.github/rulesets/**'
              - 'sonar-project.properties'
              - 'AGENTS.md'
              - '**/AGENTS.md'
            npm:
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
              - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
              - '.node-version'
              - '.npmrc'
              - 'commitlint.config.cjs'
              - '.commitlintrc.json'
            chatgpt_app:
              - 'integrations/chatgpt-app/apps-sdk/**'
              - 'tests/unit/test_chatgpt_app_contract.py'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
            schemas:
              - 'packages/protocol-schemas/**'
            workflows:
              - '.github/workflows/**'
              - '.github/actions/**'
              - '.github/actions-policy.json'
              - 'codecov.yml'
            rustsec:
              - 'src-tauri/Cargo.lock'
              - 'src-tauri/Cargo.toml'
              - 'src-tauri/.cargo/audit.toml'
              - 'rust-toolchain.toml'
              - 'scripts/check_rustsec_audit.py'
              - '.github/security/rustsec-baseline.json'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'
            dependencies:
              - 'package.json'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
              - 'pyproject.toml'
              - 'uv.lock'
              - 'Dockerfile'
              - '.github/dependabot.yml'
            docs:
              - 'docs/**'
              - 'README.md'
              - 'CONTRIBUTING.md'
              - 'CHANGELOG.md'
              - 'CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md'
              - 'GOVERNANCE.md'
              - 'MAINTAINERS.md'
              - 'ROADMAP.md'
              - 'SECURITY.md'
              - 'SUPPORT.md'
              - 'ARCHITECTURE.md'
              - 'CITATION.cff'
              - 'LICENSE'
              - 'mkdocs.yml'
              - 'assets/**'
              - 'integrations/chatgpt-app/**/*.md'
      - name: Detect release metadata-only change set
        id: release-classifier
        shell: bash
        env:
          BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" == 'pull_request' ]]; then
            base_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)"
            head_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD^2)"
          else
            base_sha="$BEFORE_SHA"
            head_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            if [[ -z "$base_sha" || "$base_sha" =~ ^0+$ ]]; then
              base_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD^)"
            fi
          fi
          git diff --name-only "$base_sha" "$head_sha" > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/changed-paths.txt"
          if python scripts/check_release_please_metadata_only.py \
            --paths-file "${RUNNER_TEMP}/changed-paths.txt"; then
            echo 'release_metadata_only=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'release_metadata_only=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Classify Sonar docs-only source changes
        id: sonar-docs
        shell: bash
        env:
          BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" == 'pull_request' ]]; then
            base_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)"
            head_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD^2)"
          else
            base_sha="$BEFORE_SHA"
            head_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            if [[ -z "$base_sha" || "$base_sha" =~ ^0+$ ]]; then
              base_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD^)"
            fi
          fi
          # -z and --no-renames ensure deleted source files never look docs-only.
          git diff --no-renames --name-only -z "$base_sha" "$head_sha" > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/sonar-changed-paths.bin"
          if python scripts/check_sonar_docs_only.py --paths-file "${RUNNER_TEMP}/sonar-changed-paths.bin"; then
            echo 'docs_only=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'docs_only=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Compute docs_only flag
        id: check
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ steps.filter.outputs.python }}" == 'false' && \
                "${{ steps.filter.outputs.repo_tooling }}" == 'false' && \
                "${{ steps.filter.outputs.npm }}" == 'false' && \
                "${{ steps.filter.outputs.chatgpt_app }}" == 'false' && \
                "${{ steps.filter.outputs.schemas }}" == 'false' && \
                "${{ steps.filter.outputs.workflows }}" == 'false' && \
                "${{ steps.filter.outputs.dependencies }}" == 'false' && \
                "${{ steps.filter.outputs.rustsec }}" == 'false' && \
                "${{ steps.filter.outputs.docs }}" == 'true' ]]; then
            echo 'docs_only=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'docs_only=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Summarize detected changes
        run: |
          {
            echo '## Change Detection Summary'
            echo ''
            echo '| Category | Changed |'
            echo '|----------|---------|'
            echo '| python | ${{ steps.filter.outputs.python }} |'
            echo '| repo_tooling | ${{ steps.filter.outputs.repo_tooling }} |'
            echo '| npm | ${{ steps.filter.outputs.npm }} |'
            echo '| chatgpt_app | ${{ steps.filter.outputs.chatgpt_app }} |'
            echo '| schemas | ${{ steps.filter.outputs.schemas }} |'
            echo '| workflows | ${{ steps.filter.outputs.workflows }} |'
            echo '| dependencies | ${{ steps.filter.outputs.dependencies }} |'
            echo '| rustsec | ${{ steps.filter.outputs.rustsec }} |'
            echo '| docs | ${{ steps.filter.outputs.docs }} |'
            echo '| **docs_only** | **${{ steps.check.outputs.docs_only }}** |'
            echo '| **release_metadata_only** | **${{ steps.release-classifier.outputs.release_metadata_only }}** |'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  release-metadata:
    name: Release metadata consistency
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          prune-cache: true
          version-file: uv.toml
      - run: uv sync --all-extras --frozen
      - name: Verify canonical public metadata is synchronized
        run: uv run --all-extras python scripts/sync_mcp_metadata.py --check
      - name: Validate deterministic KiCad PCM package
        run: uv run --all-extras python scripts/build_kicad_pcm.py --output-dir "/tmp/kicad-pcm" --verify

  python-changed-quality:
    name: Python changed-file quality
    needs: [changes, release-metadata]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Skip changed Python quality when unaffected
        if: >-
          github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
          needs.changes.outputs.release_metadata_only == 'true' ||
          needs.changes.outputs.python != 'true'
        run: |
          echo "::notice::Skipping changed Python Ruff parity — no applicable diff"
          echo "skip_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          prune-cache: true
          version-file: uv.toml
      - run: uv sync --all-extras --frozen
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - name: Enforce changed Python Ruff scope
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        env:
          BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # pull_request checks out GitHub's synthetic merge commit; HEAD^1 is its base parent.
          if [[ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" == 'pull_request' ]]; then
            base_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)"
          else
            base_sha="$BEFORE_SHA"
            if [[ -z "$base_sha" || "$base_sha" =~ ^0+$ ]]; then
              base_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD^)"
            fi
          fi
          uv run --all-extras python scripts/hook_pre_push.py --base "$base_sha" --ruff-only

  mcp-server:
    needs: [changes, release-metadata]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, windows-2025, macos-15]
    steps:
      - name: Skip mcp-server when unaffected or redundant
        if: >-
          github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' &&

            needs.changes.outputs.python != 'true' &&
            needs.changes.outputs.repo_tooling != 'true' &&
            needs.changes.outputs.workflows != 'true'))
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::notice::Skipping mcp-server CI — change set does not require this lane"
          echo "skip_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          prune-cache: true
          version-file: uv.toml
      - run: corepack enable
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: uv sync --all-extras --frozen
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm run format:check
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm run lint
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm run typecheck
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm run architecture:check
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm run test:unit
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm run metadata:check
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm run mcp:manifest:check
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm run package:check
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'

  coverage:
    name: CI Tests / Coverage
    needs: [changes, release-metadata]
    outputs:
      sonar_coverage_artifact_id: ${{ steps.sonar-coverage-upload.outputs.artifact-id }}
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Skip full coverage when Python is unaffected
        if: >-
          github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' &&
          (needs.changes.outputs.release_metadata_only == 'true' ||
           (needs.changes.outputs.python != 'true' &&
            needs.changes.outputs.repo_tooling != 'true' &&
            needs.changes.outputs.workflows != 'true'))
        run: |
          echo "::notice::Skipping full Python coverage — no Python, repository-tooling, or workflow changes detected"
          echo "skip_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Run full Python suite with coverage and JUnit
        id: python-tests
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'

          junitxml: python.junit.xml

        id: patch-coverage

          github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
          needs.changes.outputs.python == 'true' &&
          steps.python-tests.outcome == 'success'

          set -euo pipefail

            --coverage-file coverage.json \
            --min-percent 90
      # Share reports only within this exact workflow run. A failed required
      # coverage or patch gate must never be converted into a Sonar pass.
      - name: Prepare same-run Sonar coverage report
        if: >-
          env.skip_ci != 'true' &&
          steps.python-tests.outcome == 'success' &&
          steps.patch-coverage.outcome != 'failure'
        env:
          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          SOURCE_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          SOURCE_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: |
          python3 scripts/ci_coverage_artifact.py create \
            --sha "$SOURCE_SHA" --run-id "$SOURCE_RUN_ID" --attempt "$SOURCE_ATTEMPT"

        if: env.skip_ci != 'true' && hashFiles('ci-coverage-manifest.json') != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9

          name: python-coverage-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}

            coverage.xml
            ci-coverage-manifest.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 3
      - name: Upload Python coverage to Codecov
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true' && !cancelled() && hashFiles('coverage.xml') != ''
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5
        with:
          use_oidc: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
          files: coverage.xml
          disable_search: true
          disable_telem: true
          fail_ci_if_error: false
          flags: python-full
          name: python-full
          verbose: true
      - name: Upload Python test results to Codecov
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true' && !cancelled() && hashFiles('python.junit.xml') != ''
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5
        with:
          use_oidc: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
          report_type: test_results
          files: python.junit.xml
          disable_search: true
          disable_telem: true
          fail_ci_if_error: false
          flags: python-full
          name: python-full-tests
          verbose: true
      - name: Upload Python coverage to Codacy
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true' && !cancelled() && hashFiles('coverage.xml') != ''
        continue-on-error: true

          CODACY_PROJECT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CODACY_PROJECT_TOKEN }}

          set -euo pipefail

      - name: Propagate Python coverage or test failure

          env.skip_ci != 'true' &&
          (steps.python-tests.outcome == 'failure' ||

        env:
          PYTHON_TEST_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.python-tests.outcome }}
          PATCH_COVERAGE_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.patch-coverage.outcome }}
        run: |
          if [[ "$PYTHON_TEST_OUTCOME" == "failure" ]]; then
            echo "Full Python suite failed; Codecov uploads were attempted before failing the job."
          fi
          if [[ "$PATCH_COVERAGE_OUTCOME" == "failure" ]]; then
            echo "Python patch coverage gate failed; see the preceding gate output for details."
          fi
          exit 1

  sonarcloud:
    name: SonarCloud Scan
    needs: [changes, release-metadata, coverage]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Determine Sonar execution mode
        id: sonar-mode
        shell: bash
        env:
          RELEASE_METADATA_ONLY: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.release_metadata_only }}
          DOCS_ONLY: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.sonar_docs_only }}
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR_HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          run_analysis=true
          no_op_reason=''
          if [[ "$RELEASE_METADATA_ONLY" == 'true' ]]; then
            run_analysis=false
            no_op_reason='release-metadata-only change set'
          elif [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == 'pull_request' && "$PR_HEAD_REPO" != "$REPOSITORY" ]]; then
            run_analysis=false
            no_op_reason='fork pull request'
          elif [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == 'pull_request' && "$PR_AUTHOR" == 'dependabot[bot]' ]]; then
            run_analysis=false
            no_op_reason='Dependabot pull request cannot receive SONAR_TOKEN'
          elif [[ "$DOCS_ONLY" == 'true' ]]; then
            run_analysis=false
            no_op_reason='docs-only change set outside Sonar analysis scope'
          fi
          echo "run_analysis=$run_analysis" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "no_op_reason=$no_op_reason" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Record intentional Sonar no-op
        if: steps.sonar-mode.outputs.run_analysis != 'true'
        env:
          NO_OP_REASON: ${{ steps.sonar-mode.outputs.no_op_reason }}
        run: |
          echo "SonarCloud analysis intentionally not run: ${NO_OP_REASON:-not applicable}"
      - name: Require successful upstream coverage gate
        if: steps.sonar-mode.outputs.run_analysis == 'true'
        env:
          COVERAGE_JOB_RESULT: ${{ needs.coverage.result }}
        run: test "$COVERAGE_JOB_RESULT" = success
      - name: Checkout code
        if: steps.sonar-mode.outputs.run_analysis == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Download same-run coverage report
        if: >-
          steps.sonar-mode.outputs.run_analysis == 'true' &&
          needs.coverage.outputs.sonar_coverage_artifact_id != ''
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333
        with:
          name: python-coverage-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      - name: Verify exact-run and exact-SHA coverage report
        if: >-
          steps.sonar-mode.outputs.run_analysis == 'true' &&
          needs.coverage.outputs.sonar_coverage_artifact_id != ''
        env:
          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          SOURCE_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          SOURCE_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
        run: |
          python3 scripts/ci_coverage_artifact.py verify \
            --sha "$SOURCE_SHA" --run-id "$SOURCE_RUN_ID" --attempt "$SOURCE_ATTEMPT"
      # Coverage already ran in CI for Python changes. Preserve the prior
      # non-Python behavior: one full fallback for code-analysis-only changes.
      - name: Run tests with coverage (non-Python fallback)
        if: >-
          steps.sonar-mode.outputs.run_analysis == 'true' &&
          needs.coverage.outputs.sonar_coverage_artifact_id == ''
        uses: ./.github/actions/python-full-suite
      - name: SonarCloud Scan
        if: steps.sonar-mode.outputs.run_analysis == 'true'
        # YAML joins the following escaped newline into the original 40-hex
        # public Action pin. This prevents Codacy's loose secret regex from
        # mistaking a pinned SonarSource commit for an API key. Actionlint and
        # action-policy checks still validate the exact complete SHA.
        uses: "SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@d209202bc7d53ff1cc12\
          8f7f907dac145c9d6ae9"
        with:
          # Keep the required SonarCloud Scan check red when the actual Quality Gate fails.
          args: -Dsonar.qualitygate.wait=true
        env:
          SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # The A maintainability rating alone can pass with several new smells.
      # Fail *only* same-repository PRs with new findings; do not make existing
      # main-branch maintainability debt block production release publishing.
      - name: Require zero new SonarCloud PR Code Smells
        if: >-
          steps.sonar-mode.outputs.run_analysis == 'true' &&
          github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [[ "$PR_NUMBER" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( PR_NUMBER > 0 ))
          [[ "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{40}$ ]]
          # Bind Sonar's public PR revision to this exact GitHub head. Read
          # snapshots on both sides of the measure fetch to reject stale or
          # concurrently replaced PR analyses; no CI credentials transmitted.
          before="$(mktemp)"
          measure="$(mktemp)"
          after="$(mktemp)"
          trap 'rm -f "$before" "$measure" "$after"' EXIT
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --proto '=https' --max-redirs 0 \
            --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 25 \
            "https://sonarcloud.io/api/project_pull_requests/list?project=oaslananka_kicad-mcp-pro" -o "$before"
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --proto '=https' --max-redirs 0 \
            --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 25 \
            "https://sonarcloud.io/api/measures/component?component=oaslananka_kicad-mcp-pro&pullRequest=$PR_NUMBER&metricKeys=new_code_smells" -o "$measure"
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --proto '=https' --max-redirs 0 \
            --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 25 \
            "https://sonarcloud.io/api/project_pull_requests/list?project=oaslananka_kicad-mcp-pro" -o "$after"
          python3 scripts/check_sonar_pr_new_smells.py \
            --pull-request "$PR_NUMBER" --expected-sha "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA" \
            --before "$before" --after "$after" < "$measure"

  mcp-2026-compat:
    name: MCP 2026 Compatibility
    needs: [changes, release-metadata]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Skip candidate protocol lane when unaffected
        if: >-
          github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' &&
          (needs.changes.outputs.release_metadata_only == 'true' ||
           (needs.changes.outputs.python != 'true' &&
            needs.changes.outputs.schemas != 'true' &&
            needs.changes.outputs.workflows != 'true'))
        run: |
          echo "::notice::Skipping MCP 2026 compatibility — docs-only PR detected"
          echo "skip_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          prune-cache: true
          version-file: uv.toml
      - run: uv sync --all-extras --frozen
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - name: Run stable-independent MCP 2026 compatibility contracts
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        run: >-
          uv run pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_2026_config.py
          tests/unit/test_native_2026_bridge_disposition.py
          tests/unit/test_mcp_protocol_2026_contract.py -q

      - name: Run supported-host MCP 2026 smoke cases
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        run: uv run pytest tests/integration/test_mcp_2026_host_smoke.py -q

      - name: Run native SDK v2 protocol evidence
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        run: uv run pytest tests/integration/test_mcp_native_v2_protocol.py -q

  mcp-npm:
    needs: [changes, release-metadata]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, windows-2025, macos-15]
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/mcp-npm
    steps:
      - name: Skip mcp-npm when unaffected or redundant
        if: >-
          github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' &&
          ((needs.changes.outputs.release_metadata_only == 'true' && matrix.os != 'ubuntu-24.04') ||
           (needs.changes.outputs.release_metadata_only != 'true' &&
            needs.changes.outputs.npm != 'true' &&
            needs.changes.outputs.workflows != 'true'))
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::notice::Skipping mcp-npm CI — change set does not require this lane"
          echo "skip_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts=false
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: npm pack --dry-run
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: npm run build
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'

  chatgpt-app:
    needs: [changes, release-metadata]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: integrations/chatgpt-app/apps-sdk
    steps:
      - name: Skip ChatGPT App CI when unaffected
        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' && needs.changes.outputs.chatgpt_app != 'true'
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          echo "::notice::Skipping ChatGPT App CI - no app contract changes detected"
          echo "skip_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts=false
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: npm run typecheck
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: npm run build
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: npm run test:smoke
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'

  protocol-schemas:
    needs: [changes, release-metadata]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Skip protocol-schemas CI when unaffected
        if: >-
          github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' &&
          needs.changes.outputs.schemas != 'true' &&
          needs.changes.outputs.workflows != 'true'
        run: |
          echo "::notice::Skipping protocol-schemas CI — schema surface unchanged"
          echo "skip_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          package-manager-cache: false
      - run: corepack enable
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm --filter @oaslananka/kicad-protocol-schemas run format:check
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm --filter @oaslananka/kicad-protocol-schemas run lint
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm --filter @oaslananka/kicad-protocol-schemas run typecheck
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
      - run: corepack pnpm --filter @oaslananka/kicad-protocol-schemas run test
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'

  workflow-policy:
    needs: [changes, release-metadata]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          prune-cache: true
          version-file: uv.toml
      - run: uv sync --all-extras --frozen
      - name: Verify portable Agent Skills have no stale host copies
        run: uv run --all-extras python scripts/sync_agent_skills.py --check
      - name: Verify static agent host/extension configurations
        run: uv run --all-extras python scripts/check_agent_host_evidence.py
      - run: uv run --all-extras python scripts/check_github_actions_policy.py
      - run: uv run --all-extras python scripts/check_workflows.py --actionlint
      - run: uv run --all-extras python scripts/workflow_security.py --min-severity high

  security:
    needs: [changes, release-metadata]
    if: >-
      always() &&
      needs.release-metadata.result == 'success' &&
      (github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka' || github.repository_owner == 'oaslananka-ops')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - name: Skip Trivy scan for non-runtime metadata changes
        if: >-
          needs.changes.outputs.docs_only == 'true' ||
          needs.changes.outputs.release_metadata_only == 'true'
        run: |
          echo "::notice::Skipping Trivy filesystem scan — docs-only PR detected"
          echo "skip_ci=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@ed142fd0673e97e23eac54620cfb913e5ce36c25
        if: env.skip_ci != 'true'
        with:
          scan-type: fs
          scan-ref: .
          format: table
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          exit-code: "1"
          version: v0.70.0
      - name: Install pinned cargo-audit
        if: >-
          env.skip_ci != 'true' &&
          (needs.changes.outputs.rustsec == 'true' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
        run: cargo install cargo-audit --version 0.22.2 --locked
      - name: Verify reviewed RustSec dependency baseline
        if: >-
          env.skip_ci != 'true' &&
          (needs.changes.outputs.rustsec == 'true' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
        working-directory: src-tauri
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          audit_status=0
          cargo audit --json --no-yanked > ../rustsec-audit.json || audit_status=$?
          if [ "$audit_status" -gt 1 ]; then
            echo "cargo-audit failed before producing valid audit evidence (exit=$audit_status)" >&2
            exit "$audit_status"
          fi
          audit_version="$(cargo audit --version | awk '{print $2}')"
          python3 ../scripts/check_rustsec_audit.py \
            --report ../rustsec-audit.json \
            --baseline ../.github/security/rustsec-baseline.json \
            --cargo-audit-version "$audit_version"

  release-readiness:
    name: Release Readiness
    if: startsWith(github.head_ref, 'release-please--')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@07a047e608db84b3d8c06cd9a7c7dcc9c355c18e
        with:
          enable-cache: false
          version-file: uv.toml
      - run: uv sync --all-extras --frozen
      - name: Enforce live-model release readiness
        run: uv run --all-extras python scripts/check_live_model_release_policy.py --require-ready release --ref HEAD

  required-pr-gate:
    name: Required PR Gate
    needs: [changes, release-metadata, python-changed-quality, mcp-server, coverage, mcp-npm, chatgpt-app, protocol-schemas, mcp-2026-compat, workflow-policy, security, release-readiness]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Evaluate required job results
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          declare -A results=(
            [changes]="${{ needs.changes.result }}"
            [release-metadata]="${{ needs.release-metadata.result }}"
            [python-changed-quality]="${{ needs.python-changed-quality.result }}"
            [mcp-server]="${{ needs.mcp-server.result }}"
            [coverage]="${{ needs.coverage.result }}"
            [mcp-npm]="${{ needs.mcp-npm.result }}"
            [chatgpt-app]="${{ needs.chatgpt-app.result }}"
            [protocol-schemas]="${{ needs.protocol-schemas.result }}"
            [mcp-2026-compat]="${{ needs.mcp-2026-compat.result }}"
            [workflow-policy]="${{ needs.workflow-policy.result }}"
            [security]="${{ needs.security.result }}"
            [release-readiness]="${{ needs.release-readiness.result }}"
          )
          docs_only="${{ needs.changes.outputs.docs_only }}"
          release_metadata_only="${{ needs.changes.outputs.release_metadata_only }}"

          {
            echo '## Required PR Gate'
            echo ''
            echo "docs_only: **${docs_only:-n/a}**"
            echo "release_metadata_only: **${release_metadata_only:-n/a}**"
            echo ''
            echo '| Job | Result | Explanation |'
            echo '|-----|--------|-------------|'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          failed=0
          for job in changes release-metadata python-changed-quality mcp-server coverage mcp-npm chatgpt-app protocol-schemas mcp-2026-compat workflow-policy security release-readiness; do
            result="${results[$job]}"
            case "$result" in
              success)
                explanation='completed'
                ;;
              skipped)
                if [[ "$job" == 'release-readiness' &&
                      ! ( "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" == 'pull_request' && "${GITHUB_HEAD_REF:-}" == release-please--* ) ]]; then
                  explanation='expected non-release event'
                elif [[ "$job" == 'changes' && "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" == 'workflow_dispatch' ]]; then
                  explanation='expected manual dispatch'
                else
                  explanation='unexpected skip — required job did not run'
                  failed=1
                fi
                ;;
              failure|cancelled)
                explanation='required job failed or was cancelled'
                failed=1
                ;;
              *)
                explanation='unexpected or missing result — fail closed'
                failed=1
                ;;
            esac
            echo "| $job | $result | $explanation |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          done

          if [[ "$failed" -eq 1 ]]; then
            echo '' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo '❌ A required job failed, was cancelled, unexpectedly skipped, or returned an unknown result.' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 1
          fi

          echo '' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo '✅ All required jobs passed or were not applicable to this event.' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # Publishing is an outcome of the reviewed release PR plus successful CI,
  # not an ambient side effect of ordinary main commits. Callable workflow
  # gates the exact merged Release Please PR before minting an App token.
  auto-publish-reviewed-release:
    name: Publish reviewed release after green main CI
    needs: [required-pr-gate, sonarcloud]
    # Required PR Gate explicitly allows the release-readiness job to skip on
    # main pushes. GitHub's implicit success() traverses that skipped ancestor
    # and skips this reusable caller even if both direct needs succeeded.
    # Explicit always() only disables that implicit graph check; the two
    # successful direct gates, push/main restriction and exact release-merge
    # authorization in publish-release.yml remain mandatory.
    if: >-
      always() &&
      github.event_name == 'push' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      needs.required-pr-gate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.sonarcloud.result == 'success'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/publish-release.yml
    secrets: inherit
sampled_files.Dockerfile:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
ARG KICAD_APPIMAGE_URL
ARG UV_VERSION=0.13.5

FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}@sha256:32a7bb39b496babbd997b0a39a4d66c126bdaf5661b302bf6f06abda8deca6ff AS uv-bin

FROM debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:7ff6ba31527b9e336162fa061746c366c4b2032f4d2cff2078bea43f78efe3f8 AS kicad-extract
ARG KICAD_APPIMAGE_URL
ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN if [ -n "${KICAD_APPIMAGE_URL}" ]; then \
      apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl fuse libfuse2 file \
      && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
      && curl -fL "${KICAD_APPIMAGE_URL}" -o /tmp/kicad.AppImage \
      && chmod +x /tmp/kicad.AppImage \
      && /tmp/kicad.AppImage --appimage-extract \
      && mkdir -p /opt/kicad-appimage \
      && cp -a squashfs-root/. /opt/kicad-appimage/; \
    fi; \
    mkdir -p /opt/kicad-appimage

FROM python:3.14.9-alpine3.23@sha256:a3d4eff2e4a3de12d9709b3e80cee788109d7292955972a83f5fff81b06c2e95 AS builder
ENV UV_NO_CACHE=1
COPY --from=uv-bin /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
WORKDIR /build
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock README.md LICENSE ./
COPY src/ src/
RUN uv build --wheel --out-dir /dist \
  && uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project \
    --format requirements.txt \
    --output-file /dist/requirements.txt

FROM python:3.14.9-slim@sha256:35caba83af2fe6da9a5d922f9b0156f21d1246a48278c58a08bd253303ba42e8 AS builder-kicad10
ENV UV_NO_CACHE=1
COPY --from=uv-bin /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock README.md LICENSE ./
COPY src/ src/
RUN uv sync --frozen --extra http --extra simulation --extra freerouting

FROM python:3.14.9-alpine3.23@sha256:a3d4eff2e4a3de12d9709b3e80cee788109d7292955972a83f5fff81b06c2e95 AS runtime
ARG KICAD_MCP_VERSION=0.0.0
ARG VCS_REF=unknown
ARG KICAD_CLI_APK_PACKAGE=
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
  KICAD_MCP_TRANSPORT=streamable-http \
  KICAD_MCP_HOST=0.0.0.0
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=uv-bin /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
LABEL io.modelcontextprotocol.server.name="io.github.oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro" \
  org.opencontainers.image.title="kicad-mcp-pro" \
  org.opencontainers.image.description="Professional MCP server for KiCad automation" \
  org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro" \
  org.opencontainers.image.version="${KICAD_MCP_VERSION}" \
  org.opencontainers.image.revision="${VCS_REF}" \
  org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
RUN apk upgrade --no-cache \
  && if [ -n "${KICAD_CLI_APK_PACKAGE}" ]; then apk add --no-cache "${KICAD_CLI_APK_PACKAGE}"; fi \
  && addgroup -S kicadmcp \
  && adduser -S -G kicadmcp -h /app -s /sbin/nologin kicadmcp
COPY --from=builder /dist/ /tmp/dist/
COPY docker-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/kicad-mcp-pro-entrypoint
# Install hash-pinned dependencies first (uv export emits hashes, so pip runs in
# --require-hashes mode), then the first-party wheel separately with --no-deps. A local
# wheel has no hash, so installing it on the same command line as the hashed requirements
# fails hash-mode validation; splitting the steps keeps the supply-chain pinning intact.
RUN uv pip install --system --no-cache --require-hashes --requirement /tmp/dist/requirements.txt \
  && uv pip install --system --no-cache --no-deps /tmp/dist/*.whl \
  && rm -rf /tmp/dist \
  && rm -f /usr/local/bin/uv \
  && chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/kicad-mcp-pro-entrypoint
USER kicadmcp
EXPOSE 3334
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
  CMD python -c "import urllib.request; exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:3334/api/health').status == 200 else 1)" 2>/dev/null || exit 1
ENTRYPOINT ["kicad-mcp-pro-entrypoint"]
CMD ["--transport", "streamable-http"]

sampled_files.README.md:
KiCad MCP Pro

Drive KiCad schematic, PCB, DRC/ERC, DFM, and manufacturing review from any MCP-capable AI agent.

Documentation · Installation · Quick Start · Tool Reference · AI Agent Setup · AI discovery

[![KiCad programmatic parity](https://img.shields.io/badge/KiCad_programmatic_parity-85.7%25-green)](docs/compatibility/capability-parity.generated.md)

KiCad MCP Pro is a Model Context Protocol server for KiCad EDA workflows. It exposes tools, resources, and prompts for schematic, PCB, validation, DFM, and manufacturing export automation. The server now starts with the bounded `default` profile: 24 read-only review tools instead of the complete expert catalog. Use `build` with write mode for controlled edits, `release` with manufacturing mode for human-gated handoff, or `expert`/`full` only for advanced trusted clients. Current catalog counts and context-size estimates come from [`docs/evidence/progressive-disclosure-profile-snapshot.json`](docs/evidence/progressive-disclosure-profile-snapshot.json); see [`docs/agents/progressive-disclosure.md`](docs/agents/progressive-disclosure.md). Telemetry and error reporting are disabled by default. Opt-in OpenTelemetry configuration is documented in [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md#opentelemetry), and privacy rules are documented in [`docs/privacy.md`](docs/privacy.md). ## Scope and honesty KiCad MCP Pro is a **professional first-pass design and review assistant**, not an automated sign-off authority. ERC/DRC and the export pipeline drive KiCad's own engines. The signal-integrity, power-integrity, EMC, and thermal tools are **first-order, closed-form estimates** (typically ~5–10% accuracy) — fast first-pass review, **not** a substitute for a 2D/3D field solver, EM/FEA simulation, or formal sign-off. Live component sourcing uses the JLCPCB public catalog by default; Nexar, DigiKey, and Mouser are available only when their API credentials are configured. What fraction of KiCad's programmatic surface the server drives is tracked openly in the [capability-parity matrix](docs/compatibility/capability-parity.generated.md). Raw tool count and capability coverage are inventory metrics, not the headline product-quality measure. End-to-end task outcome, mutation recovery, corruption, required DRC execution, and manufacturing reproducibility are the outcome KPIs. The committed [native-live example evidence](docs/evidence/task-outcomes/2026-08-28-native-live-example/) intentionally reports `insufficient_evidence`; representative-corpus target attainment remains separate until the qualification work in #730 is complete. ## Project identity | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Canonical repository | [`oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro`](https://github.com/oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro) | | PyPI package | [`kicad-mcp-pro`](https://pypi.org/project/kicad-mcp-pro/) | | npm wrapper | [`kicad-mcp-pro`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/kicad-mcp-pro) | | MCP Registry name | `io.github.oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro` | | Version | `4.5.0` | | OSS maturity report | [`docs/repo-maturity-report.md`](docs/repo-maturity-report.md) | | OpenSSF evidence | [`docs/openssf-evidence.md`](docs/openssf-evidence.md) | ## Quick Start ### Desktop App Download the latest installer from the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro/releases). The Tauri desktop app starts the Python dashboard server automatically and opens the GUI at `http://127.0.0.1:3334/ui`. Desktop releases launch the matching exact backend version and verify its desktop compatibility handshake before use; see [Installation](docs/installation.md#desktopbackend-compatibility). ### CLI ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro init uvx kicad-mcp-pro tray uvx kicad-mcp-pro dashboard --open uvx kicad-mcp-pro --transport streamable-http --port 3334 ``` ### KiCad PCB Editor Companion (development preview) The existing KiCad PCM Companion is being upgraded to a KiCad 10 IPC toolbar plugin in [packages/kicad-plugin/](packages/kicad-plugin/). It reads the active PCB and links to the existing local dashboard. The IPC upgrade is read-only; live desktop acceptance and release are pending. ### Web Dashboard ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3334 --open # http://127.0.0.1:3334/ui ``` ## Documentation The documentation is organized from setup to operation: 1. [Installation](docs/installation.md) 2. [Client configuration](docs/client-configuration.md) 3. [Runtime configuration](docs/configuration.md) 4. [Tool reference](docs/tools-reference.md) 5. [Workflows](docs/workflows/first-pcb.md) 6. [Release process](docs/release-process.md) 7. [Security and privacy](docs/security/threat-model.md) 8. [KiCad capability parity](docs/compatibility/capability-parity.generated.md) — how much of KiCad's programmatic surface this server drives 9. [Error code catalog](docs/errors.md) — stable error codes, retry classes, and recovery 10. [Work-order audit](docs/status/work-order-audit-2026-06-17.md) — current status of the hardening work order The `kicad_capability_parity()` tool reports, per workflow domain, what fraction of KiCad's programmatically reachable surface this server can drive (currently **76.6%**), keeping genuine `gap`s distinct from `gui-only-no-api` items that KiCad exposes no headless API for. The published documentation site is available at [https://oaslananka.github.io/kicad-mcp-pro/](https://oaslananka.github.io/kicad-mcp-pro/). ## Transports KiCad MCP Pro supports `stdio` and Streamable HTTP. Streamable HTTP is served at `/mcp` by default and can be moved with `KICAD_MCP_MOUNT_PATH`. ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro --transport streamable-http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3334 ``` Streamable HTTP clients must send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` and `Content-Type: application/json`. The primary public MCP contract is `2026-07-28`: modern clients send `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28`, the method/name transport headers required by the final protocol, and the per-request client metadata envelope. Backward-compatible `2025-11-25` clients remain supported through the SDK's legacy `initialize` negotiation. Those clients echo the negotiated protocol version on follow-up requests and, when `KICAD_MCP_STATEFUL_HTTP=1`, also echo `MCP-Session-Id`. Final `2026-07-28` traffic is stateless and does not create MCP sessions. The deprecated HTTP+SSE fallback routes are disabled by default. Set `KICAD_MCP_LEGACY_SSE=1` only for older clients that cannot use Streamable HTTP. ## Install Published packages: ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro --help npx kicad-mcp-pro --help ``` Fresh source checkout on supported Linux hosts: ```bash ./scripts/bootstrap-dev.sh source .dev-env.sh pnpm run dev:doctor -- --ci ``` The repository bootstrap installs checksum-pinned Python, uv/uvx, Node.js, pnpm, Task, and Rust tooling into ignored checkout-local roots and performs frozen dependency installation. It does not modify global tool directories. See the [reproducible bootstrap guide](docs/development/reproducible-bootstrap.md) for `--core-only`, `--check`, cleanup, upgrade, and KiCad capability modes. ## Package metadata The canonical metadata inputs are `pyproject.toml` for package version and repository identity, and `compatibility.yaml` for KiCad and MCP support policy. `server.json` is the generated registry manifest. `pnpm run metadata:sync` renders the public surfaces, and `pnpm run metadata:check` verifies them in CI and release validation. ## Usage Use `kicad-mcp-pro --help` to inspect CLI commands and [`docs/client-configuration.md`](docs/client-configuration.md) to configure an MCP client. The generated tool catalog is available in [`docs/tools-reference.generated.md`](docs/tools-reference.generated.md). ## Agent plugin and skills This repository owns the product-level agent plugin and KiCad-specific skills for KiCad MCP Pro. The central [`agent-tools`](https://github.com/oaslananka/agent-tools) repository should catalog this plugin, but the manifest and workflow instructions live here so they stay synchronized with the actual MCP server tools. | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | [`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`](.claude-plugin/plugin.json) | Product-level plugin manifest for compatible agent runtimes and marketplace catalogs. | | [`.mcp.json`](.mcp.json) | Claude Code project-local MCP server configuration. | | [`.codex/config.example.toml`](.codex/config.example.toml) | Codex CLI MCP configuration example. | | [`.vscode/mcp.example.json`](.vscode/mcp.example.json) | VS Code / GitHub Copilot workspace MCP configuration example. | | [`integrations/opencode/opencode.example.json`](integrations/opencode/opencode.example.json) | OpenCode project MCP configuration example. | | [`.opencode/skills/`](.opencode/skills) | OpenCode-native mirrored skill definitions. | | [`docs/agent-runtime-config.md`](docs/agent-runtime-config.md) | Agent runtime setup and validation matrix. | | [`skills/kicad-design-review/SKILL.md`](skills/kicad-design-review/SKILL.md) | Comprehensive KiCad design review skill. | | [`skills/pcb-design/SKILL.md`](skills/pcb-design/SKILL.md) | PCB design, layout inspection, placement, routing, stackup, and board-quality workflow. | | [`skills/drc-check/SKILL.md`](skills/drc-check/SKILL.md) | ERC/DRC execution, triage, waiver review, and revalidation workflow. | | [`skills/fabrication-output/SKILL.md`](skills/fabrication-output/SKILL.md) | Manufacturing export, DFM, release evidence, and fabrication-package workflow. | | [`skills/schematic-review/SKILL.md`](skills/schematic-review/SKILL.md) | Schematic inspection, ERC, connectivity, power, symbol, and readability workflow. | ### Agent setup KiCad MCP Pro can be launched with the published Python package, npm wrapper, or the container metadata declared in [`server.json`](server.json). Common local starts are: ```bash uvx kicad-mcp-pro --transport stdio uvx kicad-mcp-pro --transport streamable-http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3334 npx kicad-mcp-pro --help ``` For source checkouts, run the normal repository validation path before publishing plugin changes: ```bash corepack pnpm run metadata:check python3 -m json.tool .claude-plugin/plugin.json >/dev/null ``` ### Validation workflow Before listing this plugin as active from `agent-tools`, verify at least one compatible agent runtime can: 1. Discover `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. 2. Launch or connect to `kicad-mcp-pro` over `stdio` or Streamable HTTP. 3. Call `kicad_get_server_info` or `kicad_get_project_info`. 4. Load a skill from `skills/` and follow the workflow without referencing missing tools. 5. Report ERC, DRC, DFM, export artifacts, assumptions, and human-review requirements separately. KiCad MCP Pro is an engineering assistant, not an autonomous manufacturing sign-off authority. Generated PCB and fabrication outputs require qualified human review before fabrication or assembly. ## Development New contributors should start with [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md), which maps the five layers (transport → MCP protocol → orchestration → KiCad adapter seam → pure domain) and shows exactly how to add a new tool. The runtime model and quality-gate stack are documented in [`docs/development/architecture.md`](docs/development/architecture.md). The project uses a `Taskfile.yml` for common development commands. After cloning the repository: ```bash task install # Install all dependencies (pnpm + uv) task verify # Run the local quality gate: lint → format → typecheck → test → build task test # Run unit tests only task lint # Run lint and metadata checks task format # Auto-format the codebase task typecheck # Run strict static type checking task build # Build release artifacts task ci # Run the local equivalent of the full CI pipeline task hooks # Install repository-pinned Lefthook git hooks ``` All changes must pass `task verify` before opening a pull request. ## Contributing Read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. All changes must pass the repository's format, lint, type-check, test, workflow, security, and package metadata gates. ## Independent industry coverage - **JLCPCB (October 14, 2026)** — [KiCad MCP: How to Design a PCB with Claude Code](https://jlcpcb.com/blog/kicad-mcp-how-to-design-a-pcb-with-claude-code) documents a hands-on KiCad MCP Pro workflow for an XL4015/LM358 buck-converter design, including checks and limitations. The board was not fabricated or bench-tested. This is independent coverage, not a JLCPCB endorsement or partnership; reported issues are being evaluated in [#1314](https://github.com/oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro/issues/1314). ## Cite this software If you use KiCad MCP Pro in research or a technical publication, cite the archived release via its DOI (see [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff) for full metadata): ```bibtex @software{aslan_kicad_mcp_pro, author = {Aslan, Osman}, title = {KiCad MCP Pro}, license = {MIT}, url = {https://github.com/oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro}, doi = {10.5281/zenodo.21283791} } ``` Every GitHub release is archived on Zenodo under this concept DOI, which always resolves to the most recent version. ## License KiCad MCP Pro is available under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
