sampled_files.pyproject.toml:
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0", "wheel"]
# A thin wrapper over setuptools that drops checkout-only test modules from the
# built distribution. `test_skills.py` is retained as public release evidence;
# `exclude-package-data` cannot do this split because `test_*.py` files are
# package CODE, not data. See scripts/build_backend.py.
build-backend = "build_backend"
backend-path = ["scripts"]

[project]
name = "mirobody"
dynamic = ["version"]
authors = [
    {name = "Theta AI Team", email = "developer@thetahealth.ai"},
]
# The PyPI storefront line: keep it in step with the README's opening lines.
description = "Mirror your body in data: one standardized, self-hosted record of your lab reports, wearables and genetics, with every number traced to its source."
readme = "README.md"
# 3.12+ is a hard floor, not a preference: the codebase uses PEP 701 f-strings
# (nested same-type quotes, e.g. utils/config/config.py), which are a SyntaxError
# on 3.11 — the package cannot even be imported there.
requires-python = ">=3.12"
# What people actually search PyPI for; the vocabulary names are the moat.
keywords = [
    "health", "health-data", "FHIR", "LOINC", "SNOMED", "wearables",
    "lab-reports", "genomics", "MCP", "agent", "AI", "LLM",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Healthcare Industry",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Medical Science Apps.",
]
# Constraint policy (this is a LIBRARY): floors only. An upper cap needs a
# reproduced breakage documented next to it — unjustified caps just create
# resolver conflicts downstream.
#
# ── Why base is one line ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# This project ships in two forms and they want opposite things. The PyPI
# package is a LIBRARY and wants to be small enough that nobody has to think
# about it. The Docker application is a PRODUCT and wants everything in the
# box. Until 1.3.0 the pyproject described only the second: base carried the
# whole ① Collect extraction stack and three LLM SDKs, so a consumer who wanted
# ② Standardize — offline name → LOINC, UCUM units — installed 93 packages and
# 245 MB, of which mirobody itself was 29 MB.
#
# That was not merely wasteful. `mcp>=2.0.0` in base made the package
# UNINSTALLABLE alongside `langchain-mcp-adapters` (which caps `mcp<2.0.0`),
# and the downstream fix was to override this file's metadata in the consumer's
# lockfile — i.e. the contract was wrong enough that using the library required
# lying about it.
#
# So: base is what `resolve()` and the vocabulary modules actually need, which
# is numpy and nothing else (measured — `import mirobody.engine` pulls zero
# third-party packages; numpy is imported inside `OfflineResolver.__init__`).
dependencies = [
    # ② Standardize. `_bundle` and `_strtab` read the shipped offset arrays with
    # it, and the resolver builds its lookup orders from them. It went
    # undeclared for a long time and worked only because pandas (since
    # removed) happened to pull it in, i.e. `mirobody resolve` depended on a
    # transitive accident.
    "numpy",
]

[project.scripts]
# The single entry point, source checkout and PyPI install alike:
# `mirobody serve|worker|parse|resolve`, or `python -m mirobody …` where a
# console
# script may not survive (compose persists site-packages but not the venv's
# bin/). Replaces the former repo-root main.py / main_worker.py, which were
# not shipped in the wheel — a PyPI install had no way to start the server.
mirobody = "mirobody.cli:main"
# The stdio MCP server alone, for `uvx --from mirobody mirobody-mcp`; the same
# as `mirobody mcp`, which is what the MCP Registry entry (server.json) runs.
mirobody-mcp = "mirobody.mcp.stdio:main"

# ── Extras: one bracket a human types, one bucket the image installs ─────────
#
# The test for whether something deserves an extra is not "is it a separable
# concern" — it is "will somebody choose it". 1.2.2 had six extras and exactly
# one of them was ever installed by anything: `requirements.txt` reads
# `-e .[agents]`, one line, no choice. `[server]` was referenced nowhere and
# could not usefully be installed alone anyway (`mirobody serve` and `worker`
# both refuse without the agent layer). `[cn]` was referenced nowhere at all,
# and was not an axis: it bundled an object-storage backend with an LLM vendor
# SDK under a country name, while their siblings (aws.py, the OpenAI/Anthropic/
# Gemini clients) sat in `[server]` and base. `storage/factory.py` iterates
# `AbstractStorage.__subclasses__()` — aws and aliyun are peers in the code and
# were split by geography only in the packaging.
#
# Three runtime extras remain, one per question (plus [test] for working on it):
#
#   [parse]  do you also want to read documents?   <- the one real choice
#   [agent]  the agent harness as a library, without the server (1.4.0)
#   [app]    everything; this is what the image installs
[project.optional-dependencies]
# ① Collect, single-file surface: `mirobody parse labs.pdf` — a lab report in,
# standardized LOINC readings out, one model key, no database and no server.
# The extraction formats and the model clients are one extra rather than two
# because `parse` needs both and nothing else needs either: an extraction
# backend with no model cannot read a scan, and the client factory exists to
# feed the extractor.
#
# `mirobody parse` checks for this extra up front and prints what to install,
# the same way `serve`/`worker` already do for the agent layer — see
# `cli._require_extra`.
parse = [
    # Documents. Every entry here is imported by name somewhere under
    # mirobody/; a package that only *typed* a file (rarfile, py7zr — archives
    # are recognised, never opened), a second library for a job one already
    # does (pypdf beside pypdfium2 + pdfplumber), or a
    # 68 MB dependency for two functions (pandas, for turning a sheet into
    # text) has been removed — see CHANGELOG 1.4.0.
    # The one PDF library: text layer AND page rendering (`documents/extract.py`).
    "pypdfium2>=4.30.0",
    "Pillow>=11.1.0",
    # `.xlsx` read directly (file_abstract_extractor.py); the pre-2007 binary
    # `.xls` is not supported, and never was — the old xlrd fallback was not
    # installed either.
    "openpyxl>=3.1",
    # Word and PowerPoint. Both read only the modern zip-based formats, which is
    # exactly the honest boundary: `.docx`/`.pptx` are supported, and legacy
    # binary `.doc`/`.ppt` stay OUT of `SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS` rather than being
    # accepted and then refused after the upload — which is what they used to do.
    "python-docx>=1.1",
    "python-pptx>=1.0",
    # The engine's own model access, via direct SDKs. The agent FRAMEWORK stack
    # (LangChain, deepagents) is a different thing and lives in [app].
    "azure-identity>=1.15.0",  # Azure OpenAI WIF token provider (utils/config/llm.py)
    "openai>=2.11.0",
    # `_build_anthropic` did a bare `import anthropic` that only resolved
    # because langchain-anthropic dragged it in, so configuring an Anthropic key
    # without the agent layer failed at client construction.
    # Floor at 1.5, and deliberately no upper cap: the newest SDK is where the
    # newest models are supported. 1.x REMOVED `temperature`, `top_p` and
    # `top_k` from the messages API, which turned every extraction call into a
    # TypeError before a request was built — so `backends_anthropic` filters
    # parameters against the installed signature rather than a hardcoded list,
    # and the next removal costs a DEBUG line instead of an outage.
    "anthropic>=1.5",
    # Floor at 2.0: the Interactions API server dropped the legacy turn-list
    # schema (breaking change, May 2026) and now requires the 2.x 'steps' schema,
    # which only the >=2.0 SDK can send/parse. No upper cap.
    "google-genai>=2.0.0",
    # `utils/config` is on the parse path (the client factory reads config), and
    # it needs these three.
    "python-dotenv",
    # Uses only the modern YAML() API (utils/config/config.py); load+dump of
    # the real config.yaml verified on 0.19, so no upper cap.
    "ruamel.yaml>=0.17",
    "cryptography",
    # `utils/net.fetch_bounded`, the bounded downloader a library consumer
    # fetches caller-supplied URLs with.
    "aiohttp",
    # `utils/http.py` is built on Starlette's Request/Response and
    # `utils/__init__` re-exports them, so importing anything under utils needs
    # it. (FastAPI is a web *framework* and stays in [app].)
    "starlette",
    "pydantic",
    # `utils/prompts.py` — the strict Jinja renderer every prompt package uses.
    "jinja2",
]

# ③a The agent layer as a LIBRARY: the harness middleware (fault containment,
# retry governance, invalid-call repair, prompt caching), the virtual-filesystem
# backends, the checkpointer, the LLM client factory, `hitl`, the prompt renderer,
# and the tool surface (`mirobody.mcp.tool` publishes the same tools an MCP client
# sees; its schemas come from the `mcp` SDK). A consumer that runs its own
# deepagents agent installs this and nothing else — no HTTP server, no object
# stores, no mail. `mirobody.mcp.service` (serving those tools over HTTP) is [app].
agent = [
    # Calculation for a model on the person's own hardware: local containers,
    # through the maintained Docker SDK. Code never uses a remote sandbox provider.
    "docker>=7.1.0",
    # Calculation for every other model: QuickJS compiled to WebAssembly, run
    # in process on wasmtime, with no network, files or Docker (the engine
    # under deepagents' `eval` interpreter). A pure-Python wheel; 0.x, so the
    # next minor version is held back until it is tried.
    "quickjs-rs>=0.2.6,<0.3",
    # The checkpointer (langgraph-checkpoint-postgres) and the file-system
    # projections talk to Postgres directly.
    "psycopg[binary]",
    # 3.2 is the first with `check=`, which replaces a connection a Postgres
    # restart killed instead of failing the request that drew it.
    "psycopg[pool]",
    "psycopg-pool>=3.2",
    "jinja2",
    # `utils/config` — the client factory, the checkpointer and the registry
    # read configuration through it. `mirobody.utils` itself resolves its
    # re-exports lazily, so importing one helper (`utils.sse`, `utils.prompts`,
    # …) pulls none of this.
    "ruamel.yaml",
    "python-dotenv",
    "cryptography",
    # `utils/net.fetch_bounded` (see [parse]).
    "aiohttp",
    # Model clients: the two families the shipped config.yaml uses. Every other
    # family is one `pip install` away and NOT declared here: `init_chat_model`
    # imports a provider package lazily and names it in the error when it is
    # missing. So a deployment that configures `llm_type: anthropic` (deepagents
    # brings langchain-anthropic anyway), a Vertex-hosted model
    # (`langchain-google-vertexai`, which drags the 170 MB
    # `google-cloud-aiplatform` behind it) or an Azure OpenAI WIF login
    # (`azure-identity`, which [parse] carries) adds that one package — instead
    # of every install carrying all of them for a configuration it never has.
    # `langchain_community` was declared and never imported; gone.
    # 1.4.0 is deepagents 0.7.14's floor.
    "langchain>=1.4.0",
    "langchain-openai>=1.4.3",
    # 4.2.4 relaxed its google-genai cap to <3.0.0 (earlier 4.x pinned <2.0.0,
    # which would block the google-genai>=2.0 required by [parse]).
    # 4.4.0 is the version verified to round-trip Gemini 3.x's
    # `thought_signature` through a tool loop (see `gemini-flash` in
    # config.llm.yaml). No upper cap: newer packages support newer models, and
    # the one time a floor without a verified lower bound bit us, `anthropic`
    # 1.x had silently removed `temperature` from `messages.create`.
    "langchain-google-genai>=4.4.0",
    # Floor at 0.7.5. 0.7 is where the BackendProtocol settled: the deprecated
    # `*_info` / `grep_raw` shims are gone (we never used them), `glob`/`grep`
    # take `path: str | None`, `grep` gained a `max_count` cap that
    # CompositeBackend splits across mounts, and `delete` arrived as an optional
    # protocol method (PgFilesystemBackend does not implement it; the tool is
    # excluded by name — see agent/agent.py `_EXCLUDED_NATIVE_TOOLS`).
    # NOTE 0.7 also DROPPED `TodoListMiddleware` from the default middleware
    # stack, so `write_todos` no longer exists unless a caller adds it back.
    # the agent intentionally does not — see agent/agent.py `_build_agent`.
    # Floor raised to 0.7.14 on 2026-09-16; the API this repository binds
    # (`create_deep_agent`, `HarnessProfile`, the backends, `get_model_provider`)
    # is byte-identical across 0.7.5..0.7.14, and 0.7.14 pulls langchain 1.4.
    "deepagents>=0.7.19",
    # Conversation memory: the agent graph is compiled with an AsyncPostgresSaver
    # keyed on thread_id = session_id, so LangGraph replays the real message
    # objects. This replaced a hand-rolled rebuild of history from persisted UI
    # chunks (the deleted chat/history_replay.rebuild_canonical_messages) —
    # see agent/checkpointer.py.
    "langgraph-checkpoint-postgres>=3.1.2",
    # Floor at 2.0 for two reasons, both verified against the installed source
    # rather than release notes:
    #   1. 2.0.0 is the first release implementing protocol revision 2026-07-28
    #      (DiscoverRequest/Result, InputRequiredResult/MRTR, CacheHint);
    #      1.29.0 tops out at 2025-11-25.
    #   2. Its `func_metadata` generates our tool inputSchemas. The hand-rolled
    #      parser it replaced got Literal, Enum, bare dict and Annotated wrong.
    # NOTE `mcp.server.fastmcp` was REMOVED in 2.0 (it is `mcp.server.mcpserver`
    # now), and the third-party `fastmcp` package does not yet import against
    # 2.0 at all (`McpError` was renamed `MCPError`), so it is not an option.
    "mcp>=2.0.0",
]

# ③ Everything — the HTTP/chat/MCP server, its stores, and the agent layer.
# `requirements.txt` is `-e .[app]` and that is the only thing that installs
# it: `docker compose` mounts the checkout and pip-installs from it, so PyPI is
# not a deployment path and this extra never asks anyone to choose a backend.
# Both object stores and every model vendor go in, unconditionally — oss2 is
# 0.3 MB and aioboto3 0.2 MB, and a decision point costs more than that.
app = [
    "mirobody[parse]",
    "mirobody[agent]",
    # HTTP surface.
    "fastapi",
    "python-multipart",
    "uvicorn",
    # Stores.
    "sqlalchemy",
    # SQLAlchemy declares greenlet only under platform markers and extras, so
    # its async engine can be missing it on an otherwise-correct install.
    "greenlet",
    # Object storage — `storage/factory.py` tries every AbstractStorage
    # subclass and falls back to local, so which one is a config question at
    # runtime, never an install-time one.
    "aioboto3",
    "oss2",
    # boto3 is the SYNC half of `utils/config/llm.py::_build_bedrock`, and it
    # was never declared anywhere: it arrived transitively via aioboto3, which
    # is the same class of bug as the undeclared python-multipart / starlette /
    # anthropic before it. Named here so it stops being an accident.
    "boto3",
    # Identity and mail.
    "pyjwt",
    "webauthn>=2.0.0",
    "mandrill",
    # OAuth1 — among the shipped providers, only Garmin still speaks it.
    "requests-oauthlib",
]

# The suite a clone runs. CI's first job is `pip install -e '.[test]'` followed
# by `pytest -q`, which is how a minimal install that aborts at collection is
# caught; without this extra that job installs numpy and exits 127 on a missing
# pytest, which is what happened when `indicator-build` was deleted beside it.
test = ["pytest", "pytest-asyncio", "pytest-sugar", "import-linter", "ruff", "build"]


[project.urls]
"Homepage" = "https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody"
"Bug Reports" = "https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/issues"
"Source" = "https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["mirobody", "mirobody.*"]
# `mirobody/tests/` is the part of the suite in git: the resolver score the
# README publishes, the cross-language identity checks a terminology
# contributor runs, the server's security gates, and `test_skills.py`, the
# public evidence for the agent skills. The build backend ships only that evidence module and prunes the
# checkout-only gates; `scripts/check_wheel_data.py` enforces the split.
#
# Everything else lives in a gitignored `tests/` at the repo root, so the local
# regression suite can be thorough without becoming public API. That rule was
# briefly dropped on `refactor/deep-agent-only` and 92 test files reached the
# public remote; `.gitignore` carries the account.

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"mirobody" = [
    # PEP 561: without this marker every type checker ignores the annotations
    # in this package entirely, so a consumer gets `Any` for `Resolution`,
    # `ParsedQuantity` and everything else no matter how well typed it is.
    "py.typed",
    "**/*.md",
    "**/*.sql",
    "**/*.json",
    "**/*.yaml",
    "**/*.jinja",
    "**/*.so",
    # ── engine data bundles (Git LFS) ────────────────────────────────────────
    # These are not optional extras: `mirobody.engine.resolve` — the front door
    # of ② Standardize, and the one line the README leads with — reads
    # res/loinc/fhir_loinc_bundle.tar.gz and res/loinc/aliases_src/*.tsv
    # at import time. Until 1.0.62 only *.bin was listed here, so every published
    # wheel shipped an engine that could not resolve anything. Keep .gz/.npy/.tsv
    # in this list; scripts/check_wheel_data.py enforces it at build time.
    "**/*.bin",
    "**/*.gz",
    # Public, small genotype examples ship with the testing toolbox; keep
    # these globs narrow so a raw personal upload cannot enter a wheel.
    "testing/genomics/*.vcf",
    "testing/genomics/*.txt",
    "testing/genomics/*.csv",
    "testing/genomics/*.bgz",
    "testing/genomics/*.zip",
    # The read-only dbSNP site index is queried on genotype import.
    "**/*.sqlite3",
    # res/ucum/ucum-essence.xml: UCUM's own table, verbatim (its NOTICE says why).
    "**/*.xml",
    "**/*.npy",
    "**/*.tsv",
    "**/*.NOTICE",
    "**/*.html",
    "**/*.htm",
    "**/*.js",
    "**/*.css",
    "**/*.png",
    "**/*.jpg",
    "**/*.jpeg",
    "**/*.svg",
    "**/*.ico",
]
# NOTE: there is deliberately no [tool.setuptools.exclude-package-data] here.
# It does not work against the broad `**/*.bin` / `**/*.npy` includes above —
# setuptools keeps files the include globs matched — and a stanza that looks
# like it prunes 28 MB while pruning nothing is worse than none. The pruning
# lives in scripts/build_backend.py::_BUILD_ONLY_DATA (wheel) and MANIFEST.in
# (sdist), and scripts/check_wheel_data.py fails the build if it stops working.

# (The web client's static assets live at repo-root frontend/ — outside the
# package on purpose. A pip install serves API + MCP; the UI comes from a
# checkout (Docker/source) or the hosted client at mirobody.ai. This is what
# took the wheel from ~57MB of which 8MB was JavaScript, to engine + data only.)

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = {attr = "mirobody.__version__"}

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
disable_test_id_escaping_and_forfeit_all_rights_to_community_support = true
# Collect bare `async def` tests via pytest-asyncio (already in the [test]
# extra). Without this the async tests fail with "async def functions are not
# natively supported" on every machine.
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Two roots. `mirobody/tests/` holds the gates that ship: the resolver
# benchmark the README scores itself against, cross-language identity and the
# server's security gates. `tests/` is the local regression
# suite and is gitignored: internal quality control that can be as detailed as
# it needs to be without becoming part of the project's public surface. It is simply absent from a clone, and
# pytest skips a testpath that does not exist. (Historical note: the README
# once documented a tests/ directory along with `-m mcp` / `-m chat` and other
# markers, none of which existed — following it produced "0 tests collected".)
testpaths = ["mirobody", "tests"]

# into one collides every test module with its twin ("import file mismatch").
norecursedirs = [".*", "build", "dist", "node_modules", "out", "frontend", "__pycache__"]
markers = [

# ── Lint gate (run: ruff check mirobody) ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# Narrow on purpose: every rule here is either a real defect class (F: undefined
# names, unused imports/variables, duplicate definitions; B905: a zip that
# silently truncates; B006: a mutable default) or a modernisation the 3.12 floor
# makes unambiguous (UP: PEP 585/604 annotations, datetime.UTC). Style rules
# that would generate churn without catching anything (import sorting, line
# length, quote style) are deliberately absent — add one only with the diff that
# applies it.
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 120
extend-exclude = ["frontend"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Narrow by design, and every addition below earns its place by catching a class
# of DEFECT rather than a style preference:
#   B    flake8-bugbear — late-binding closures, mutable defaults, mutable
#        class attributes. B904 and B007 are ignored below.
#   ISC  implicit string concatenation — the missing comma in a list literal.
#   PLE  pylint errors. PLE0604 is excluded below: it cannot see through a
#        dynamically built `__all__`, which is how the lazy (PEP 562) packages
#        here export.
#   RUF100  a `noqa` that no longer suppresses anything. A stale one silently
#        swallows the NEXT finding on that line.
#   C4, PIE  comprehension and simplification defects, three findings between them.
#   TID  a relative import that leaves its directory (TID252, at ruff's default
#        `parents` level; plain `from .sibling` stays legal). See CLAUDE.md:
#        the same dependency was being spelled two ways, so grep stopped
#        answering "who imports kernel".
select = [
    "E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "UP",
    "B", "ISC", "C4", "PIE", "PLE", "RUF100",
    "RET505", "RET507", "PLW0602", "TID",
]
ignore = [
    "B007",   # unused loop variable. `for k, v in d.items()` when only `v` is read
              # names the key for a reader even when the code does not use it;
              # rewriting it to `.values()` is churn, not a fix. (owner, 2026-09-08)
    "B904",   # `raise ... from` inside `except`. It only changes what a traceback
              # PRINTS ("during handling of the above" vs "direct cause"), and the
              # original is in the chain either way — not worth 33 mechanical
              # edits across the tree. (owner, 2026-09-08)
    "E402",   # imports after code: three routers register models before importing helpers on purpose
    "E701",   # `if x: return` one-liners in the strtab/bundle readers
    "E741",   # `l` as a variable in a few tight loops
    "UP042",  # (str, Enum) -> StrEnum: the enum values are persisted wire strings; not worth the diff
    "PLE0604",  # `__all__` built with `*_EXPORTS`: the lazy packages compute it, and
                # the linter cannot prove the members are strings.
]
# NOT selected, each for a reason, so the next person does not re-litigate it:
#   G004 (1,110 findings) f-string in a log call. Worth doing — lazy formatting
#        and the PHI policy both want %-style — but 1,110 mechanical edits would
#        bury any real change in the same commit. Its own PR.
#   DTZ  (68) `datetime.now()` without a tz. DELIBERATE here: `series_data.time`,
#        the device point buffer, is a NAIVE LOCAL wall clock and the aggregation
#        pass is built on that (th_observation itself stores timestamptz with its
#        zone). Selecting DTZ would ask us to break the buffer's contract to
#        satisfy a linter.
# TID252 was listed here as "relative imports are used throughout by choice".
# Reversed 2026-09-14 on measurement, not taste: numpy nests deeper than we do
# with zero parent-relative imports, fastapi likewise, and nothing in an
# eighteen-library sample reached the four dots this package had. It is selected
# above now. import-linter still guards the layering; TID252 keeps the edge
# visible to a reader.

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear]
# FastAPI declares a parameter's SOURCE in its default: `file: UploadFile =
# File(...)`, `user = Depends(auth)`. B008 is right about mutable defaults in
# general and wrong about this framework's entire calling convention.
extend-immutable-calls = [
    "fastapi.File", "fastapi.Form", "fastapi.Body", "fastapi.Query",
    "fastapi.Path", "fastapi.Header", "fastapi.Cookie", "fastapi.Depends",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Package __init__ files re-export for their consumers; every import there is
# "unused" to a linter and load-bearing to the package.
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]
sampled_files.requirements.txt:
# The FULL platform — what compose.yaml and deploy.sh install. This file is the
# only thing that installs `[app]`, which is the point: the Docker application
# mounts the checkout and pip-installs from it, so PyPI is never a deployment

#
# A bare `pip install mirobody` is the LIBRARY: ② Standardize (resolve, units,
# lexical) on numpy alone. `pip install 'mirobody[parse]'` adds ① Collect's
# single-file surface. See pyproject.toml for why there are only those two.
-e .[app]

repository.readme:
# JobAppAgent: open-source AI job application agent ### Search roles, match them to one verified résumé, apply within your rules on Greenhouse, Ashby and Lever, and track confirmed submissions. [![Validate](https://github.com/vaibhavarora14/job-application-agent/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/vaibhavarora14/job-application-agent/actions/workflows/validate.yml) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/job-application-agent?logo=npm&color=CB3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/job-application-agent) [![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2563EB.svg)](LICENSE) [![Agent Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent_Skills-compatible-111827)](job-application-agent/SKILL.md) [Get started](#-get-started) · [Privacy in 30 seconds](#-privacy-in-30-seconds) · [Safety](#-safety) · [Privacy](#-privacy) · [Where to find it](#-where-to-find-it) · [Dashboard](https://job-application-agent-telemetry.varora1406.workers.dev/) · [Security](SECURITY.md)
```bash npx job-application-agent@latest install ``` ```bash npx skills add vaibhavarora14/job-application-agent ``` --- JobAppAgent (Job Application Agent) is an [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io/specification) that helps a coding agent discover, evaluate, complete, and track your own job applications. It uses one verified résumé, checks eligibility and duplicates, and records only confirmed submissions. ## 🔒 Privacy in 30 seconds - OS credential store for profile - One verified résumé; refuse unverifiable claims - Never reads cookies/session files; pauses for SSO/MFA/CAPTCHA/legal - Only records confirmed submissions (filled ≠ applied) - Analytics/community sharing opt-out via CLI ## 🚀 Get started Install it with either: ```bash npx job-application-agent@latest install ``` ```bash npx skills add vaibhavarora14/job-application-agent ``` Then tell your coding agent: ```text Use job-application-agent to onboard my résumé and job preferences. ``` After onboarding, use natural commands: ```text search jobs list discovery sources for India and global remote engineering apply https://company.example/jobs/123 apply all relevant jobs from this thread: run a round of 10 show attention queue record outcome Company — Senior Engineer — interview ``` Requires Node.js 20 or newer and a browser-capable coding agent. ### Use your preferred agent Setup templates are available for **Hermes Agent**, **Grok Bot**, and **OpenClaw**: ```bash npx job-application-agent@latest platforms npx job-application-agent@latest platforms hermes ``` Replace `hermes` with `grok` or `openclaw` for that guide. These commands print instructions only; they do not install a Bot, change agent settings, or access candidate state. Browse the [platform guides](https://jobappagent.com/platforms). Each template starts in review mode and requires browser validation on its host. The [Grok Bot template](https://x.ai/bot/0PNQABev0aiAUlhWI83XH) starts in review mode, where every submit is confirmed. The existing installer also supports Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini skill directories when present. On Linux, profile storage uses the Secret Service via the `secret-tool` CLI. Install it with `sudo apt-get install libsecret-tools` (Debian/Ubuntu) or the equivalent package manager command for your distribution. Unlike macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager, the Linux Secret Service has no always-running system daemon: a keyring daemon (GNOME Keyring, KWallet, or similar) must be running in the user session for `secret-tool` to store or read the profile. On a desktop login this is normally already the case; on headless servers, containers, or SSH-only sessions, start one explicitly (e.g. `gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock --components=secrets`) before first use. For one person's agents across several trusted hosts, an optional private Cloudflare D1 backend with R2 (or a private Workers KV blob fallback) shares profile, résumé, application, outcome, round, answer, and attention state. Each host receives a separate revocable credential, and one renewable lease ensures only one host submits applications at a time. See [`CLOUD_STATE.md`](job-application-agent/references/CLOUD_STATE.md). ## ✨ What it does | Stage | Behavior | |---|---| | **Discover** | Searches a shared, versioned catalog of direct careers, ATS platforms, networks, feeds, and job boards, then verifies every lead at the employer. | | **Qualify** | Checks seniority, skills, location, authorization, compensation, and posting status. | | **Apply** | Fills forms and uploads one canonical résumé using verified facts only. | | **Track** | Deduplicates applications and records only visible submission confirmations. | | **Improve** | Reviews outcomes and proposes targeting changes without rewriting candidate facts. | ## 🤖 Choose your autonomy level An optional [outreach companion](job-application-agent/references/OUTREACH.md) qualifies contacts, stores drafts, prepares manual handoffs, and tracks replies privately. Run `job-application-agent outreach policy status` to inspect it. It is disabled by default, performs no automated LinkedIn/X access or sending, and keeps outreach counts separate from applications. Cloud use requires the `outreach-tracking-v1` private-state migration; local use works with the managed npm installation on Node 20 or later. You approve every send. The agent fills applications but never submits them. It stages them as a review batch, and you approve that batch on a local review page, which shows the company, role, URL, fit score, every drafted answer and the résumé. On hosts without a local browser, you approve by typing a short approval phrase in chat. You can untick anything you don't want sent. Approval covers exactly what you saw, once, for 24 hours. - **`review-each`** (default): one application per review. - **`routine-auto`**: the agent batches up to 25 routine applications into one review. repository.readme:
# GSD Task Manager

A privacy-first Eisenhower matrix for deciding what to do, schedule, delegate,
or eliminate.

**Live app:** [gsd.vinny.dev](https://gsd.vinny.dev)
**Current version:** 14.3.0
**Current product:** the v11 single-matrix shell, offline-first local storage,
optional PocketBase sync, and the GSD MCP server.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/gsd-mcp-server.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/gsd-mcp-server)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/gsd-mcp-server.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/gsd-mcp-server)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

![GSD Task Manager Eisenhower matrix](public/gsd-matrix.png)

## What ships in v11

- A responsive four-quadrant matrix with drag-and-drop movement.
- Quick Capture, full task editing, search, keyboard navigation, and optional
  built-in Smart Views.
- Due dates, tags, dependency selection, and circular-dependency prevention.
- Archive, dashboard/review analytics, sync history, settings, and onboarding.
- Local IndexedDB persistence, JSON import/export, offline PWA support, and
  user-controlled update prompts.
- Optional multi-device PocketBase sync with Google, Apple, or GitHub OAuth and
  realtime server-sent events.
- A separately installed MCP server with 19 task, analytics, and diagnostic
  tools, including validated and dry-run-aware writes.
- Light and dark Inkwell "GSD Editorial" themes with WCAG AA as the
  accessibility floor.

Retired v7/v8 surfaces such as selection-mode batch operations, the Quick
Settings panel, and smart-view pinning shortcuts are not part of the v11 shell.

## Privacy and data custody

Local-only mode is the default. Tasks are stored in the browser's IndexedDB and
the core product does not require a backend. Clearing browser data can erase
local tasks, so export backups regularly.

Cloud sync is explicitly optional. When enabled, task data is sent to the
configured PocketBase server; the hosted configuration uses
`https://api.vinny.io`. Self-hosting instructions and the encryption-at-rest
hooks live under [`docker/`](docker/). See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for the
precise trust and token-storage posture.

## Using the matrix

The Eisenhower matrix classifies work by urgency and importance:

- **Do First** — urgent and important.
- **Schedule** — important, not urgent.
- **Delegate** — urgent, not important.
- **Eliminate** — neither urgent nor important.

Use the Quick Capture field or press `n` to start a task. Use `Shift+N` for the
full composer, `/` for search, `?` for help, and `Option+1` through `Option+4`
(`Alt` on non-Mac keyboards) to focus a quadrant. The in-app help drawer is the
canonical shortcut ledger.

## Saved items

Choose **Move to Saved** on an incomplete task to keep reading material or an idea
outside the matrix. Saved preserves the title, links, tags, and task context.
Use **Notes and links** for short annotations (600 characters including links),
search Saved or the command palette, and choose **Return to matrix** when ready.
Review the quadrant and due date before returning. Saved items do not contribute
to active task counts, review analytics, reminders, or due badges.

Saved works offline and travels in JSON backups. Cloud sync requires the additive
`saved_at` migration shipped with this feature before rollout. iOS support is a
follow-up: older iOS clients still treat saved items as ordinary tasks. See
[`tasks/saved-tasks/spec.md`](tasks/saved-tasks/spec.md) for the compatibility scope.

## Local development

Requirements: [Bun](https://bun.sh/) 1.3.14, [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 22.22.2+ (or 24.15+ or 26+), and a current browser. `bun run` executes package scripts on Node, so tests, lint, and builds run on your installed Node.

```bash
bun install
bun dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`. A fresh browser profile starts at `/about`; use
the **Open App** call to action to enter the matrix. PocketBase is not required
for local task CRUD.

### Canonical checks

```bash
bun run test
bun run test -- --coverage
bun typecheck
bun lint
bun run quality:shape
bun run license:check
bun audit --audit-level=high
bun run build
bun run test:e2e
```

Use `bun run test`, not `bun test`; the latter invokes Bun's built-in runner
instead of Vitest. Playwright covers Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. The optional
authenticated PocketBase harness runs with:

```bash
bun run test:system:pocketbase
```

To run the CI browser suite locally under the production CSP:

```bash
bun run build:e2e
bun run test:csp
bun run test:pwa
bun run test:e2e:export -- --workers=2
```

`build:e2e` selects the CSP-approved hosted backend at build time; feedback
tests intercept that endpoint and never submit to it. A plain local build
defaults to localhost:8090, which the production CSP intentionally blocks.
On macOS, Firefox tests use a disposable app-data home to avoid Playwright's
Firefox 157 profile-launch issue. It is removed after the browser exits;
the regular browser profile and system privacy permissions are untouched.

## Architecture

- Next.js 16 App Router static export; the application is client-side.
- React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and the Violet Frost Inkwell tokens.
- Dexie/IndexedDB for local data and PocketBase for optional cloud sync.
- Vitest for unit/integration coverage and Playwright for browser coverage.
- Bun workspaces, including [`packages/mcp-server/`](packages/mcp-server/).

Start with [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md),
[`docs/security-trust-boundaries.md`](docs/security-trust-boundaries.md), and
the architecture decisions in [`docs/adr/`](docs/adr/).

## Deployment

- `bun run build` creates the static export in `out/`.
- `bun run deploy` runs the production deployment script. Production
  (gsd.vinny.dev) is the only deploy target; the development deploy was
  retired on 2026-09-11.
- [`docker/Dockerfile`](docker/Dockerfile) builds the self-hosted Caddy and
  PocketBase image.
- [`cloudfront/response-headers-policy.json`](cloudfront/response-headers-policy.json)
  and the related scripts manage production response headers.

Uploading an artifact is not proof that the CDN or a running container serves
it. Verify the deployed URL separately.

## Release documentation checklist

Before changing the release version or announcing a feature:

1. Compare the README version with `package.json`.
2. Verify every feature claim in the current shell, not only in retained data
   models or archived ADRs.
3. Run the canonical checks above and a production static build.
4. Update the GitHub release notes, `SECURITY.md`, and the trust-boundary map
   when the release changes their claims.
5. Treat source, tests, build artifacts, deployment, and live runtime as
   separate evidence states.

## Contributing and security

Read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) before making changes. Report
vulnerabilities through the private process in [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md),
not a public issue.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]

# In-flight CI runs on the same ref get cancelled when a new push arrives.
# Saves CI minutes; safe because CI is a pure gate (no side effects).
# Deploy workflows do the opposite: cancel-in-progress: false.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14
      - name: Prefer IPv4 for npm registry
        run: echo 'precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100' | sudo tee -a /etc/gai.conf
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Typecheck
        run: bun typecheck

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14
      - name: Prefer IPv4 for npm registry
        run: echo 'precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100' | sudo tee -a /etc/gai.conf
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Lint
        run: bun lint
      - name: Enforce code-shape baseline
        run: bun run quality:shape
      - name: Check for unused files and dependencies
        run: bun run knip

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14
      # `bun run` executes Vitest on Node; pin the floor line instead of the image default.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - name: Prefer IPv4 for npm registry
        run: echo 'precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100' | sudo tee -a /etc/gai.conf
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Enforce dependency licenses and generate SBOM
        run: bun run license:check -- --sbom "$RUNNER_TEMP/gsd-taskmanager.cdx.json"
      - name: Upload dependency SBOM
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: dependency-sbom
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/gsd-taskmanager.cdx.json
          retention-days: 30
      - name: Test
        run: bun run test -- --coverage
        env:
          CI: true

  mcp-coverage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - name: Prefer IPv4 for npm registry
        run: echo 'precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100' | sudo tee -a /etc/gai.conf
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Test MCP server with coverage
        run: bun run --cwd packages/mcp-server test:coverage
        env:
          CI: true

  pocketbase-system:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14
      - name: Prefer IPv4 for npm registry
        run: echo 'precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100' | sudo tee -a /etc/gai.conf
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Install Chromium for browser/PocketBase boundary test
        uses: ./.github/actions/install-playwright
        with:
          browser: chromium
      - name: Run authenticated PocketBase system test
        run: bun run test:system:pocketbase

  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        browser: [chromium, firefox, webkit]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.14
      - name: Prefer IPv4 for npm registry
        run: echo 'precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100' | sudo tee -a /etc/gai.conf
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Install ${{ matrix.browser }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/install-playwright
        with:
          browser: ${{ matrix.browser }}
      - name: Build production export
        run: bun run build:e2e
      - name: Verify production PWA lifecycle in ${{ matrix.browser }}
        run: bun run test:pwa -- ${{ matrix.browser }}
      - name: Boot production export under strict CSP
        if: matrix.browser == 'chromium'
        run: bun run test:csp
      - name: Run end-to-end tests against the production export in ${{ matrix.browser }}
        run: bun run test:e2e:export -- --project=${{ matrix.browser }}
        env:
          CI: true
      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: playwright-report-${{ matrix.browser }}
          path: playwright-report/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/build-static-export
      - name: Enforce first-load JavaScript budget
        run: bun run quality:bundle

repository.readme:
# Academia de IA Xäboli **Rutas de aprendizaje de IA con examen y un catastro abierto, en español y vivo, de repositorios, cursos y herramientas**, clasificados por tema, con las relaciones entre ellos y recursos gratuitos de las 10 mejores universidades del mundo. 🌐 **Sitio:** [academia.xaboli.cl](https://academia.xaboli.cl) · 📈 **Actualizado:** 18 de octubre de 2026 · 🔁 **Próxima revisión:** 1 nov 2026 [![Licencia del contenido: CC BY 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/contenido-CC%20BY%204.0-blue)](LICENSE-CONTENT.md) [![Licencia del código: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/c%C3%B3digo-MIT-green)](LICENSE) [![Validación](https://github.com/xagent7/catastro-ia/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/xagent7/catastro-ia/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Enlaces](https://github.com/xagent7/catastro-ia/actions/workflows/enlaces.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/xagent7/catastro-ia/actions/workflows/enlaces.yml) | 121 recursos | 98 repositorios de GitHub | 15 categorías | 136 relaciones | 19 recursos universitarios | 1 learning path | |:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:| ## Qué lo hace distinto - **En español y para equipos de LATAM.** Cada ficha explica qué es el recurso y *para qué sirve en una ruta de aprendizaje*, no solo un enlace. - **Relaciones entre recursos.** Qué se complementa, qué es alternativa de qué y qué conviene aprender antes. En el sitio se exploran como [mapa interactivo](https://academia.xaboli.cl/#mapa). - **Honesto sobre lo que no se verificó.** Las fichas marcadas *según el proyecto* repiten lo que declaran sus autores; las que tienen riesgos (seguridad, términos de uso, afirmaciones no verificadas) llevan advertencia. - **Solo recursos directos.** Repositorios, cursos, libros, herramientas y documentación oficial. Sin artículos ni noticias. - **Vivo.** Se revisa cada mes, con verificación automática de enlaces y un registro público de cambios. - **Learning paths con examen.** Rutas por objetivo y nivel, con una práctica por módulo y un examen interactivo. ## Learning paths | Ruta | Módulos | Examen | | |---|:-:|:-:|---| | **LP8 · Ciclo de desarrollo de software con IA**
Cómo construir software con agentes de punta a punta: Claude Code y herramientas afines, bootstrap de proyectos, desarrollo guiado por especificaciones, agentes del desarrollo y CI/CD para soluciones agénticas. | 10 | 100 preguntas | [Abrir](https://academia.xaboli.cl/lp/sdlc-ia/) | Se publica una ruta nueva cada mes. Para recibir el aviso, deja tu correo al final de cualquier examen en el sitio. ## Contenido - [Fundamentos y rutas de AI Engineering](#fundamentos-y-rutas-de-ai-engineering) (11) - [LLMs desde cero y entrenamiento](#llms-desde-cero-y-entrenamiento) (7) - [Prompt y context engineering](#prompt-y-context-engineering) (5) - [Frameworks y patrones de agentes](#frameworks-y-patrones-de-agentes) (13) - [Ecosistema Google de agentes](#ecosistema-google-de-agentes) (9) - [Claude Code, skills y harness](#claude-code-skills-y-harness) (16) - [SDD y SDLC agéntico](#sdd-y-sdlc-agentico) (5) - [Comprensión de código y diagramas](#comprension-de-codigo-y-diagramas) (8) - [RAG, datos e ingesta](#rag-datos-e-ingesta) (9) - [Inferencia, modelos y gateways](#inferencia-modelos-y-gateways) (9) - [Seguridad y gobernanza de agentes](#seguridad-y-gobernanza-de-agentes) (7) - [IA multimodal y generativa](#ia-multimodal-y-generativa) (4) - [Apps e interfaces para agentes](#apps-e-interfaces-para-agentes) (2) - [Plataformas de formación](#plataformas-de-formacion) (11) - [Certificación Claude](#certificacion-claude) (5) - [Universidades top 10 (QS 2026)](#universidades-top-10-qs-2026) (19) - [Novedades](#novedades) > **Leyenda.** ✅ descripción contrastada · 🔎 según el proyecto (lo que declaran sus autores) · ⚠️ tiene advertencia · 🆕 agregado en los últimos 60 días ## Fundamentos y rutas de AI Engineering Currículos, roadmaps e índices para aprender IA de forma ordenada. | Recurso | Tipo · nivel | Para qué sirve | |---|---|---| | ✅ [**microsoft/AI-For-Beginners**](https://github.com/microsoft/AI-For-Beginners)
Curso de Microsoft de 12 semanas y 24 lecciones sobre IA clásica y moderna: IA simbólica, redes neuronales, visión por computadora, procesamiento de lenguaje natural y ética. Cada lección incluye notebooks en PyTorch y TensorFlow, cuestionarios y laboratorios. | Repo · curso · Principiante | Es la base para una audiencia sin formación previa, por ejemplo en un programa de adopción para equipos no técnicos.

sampled_files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: Validación
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  validar:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Validar datos
        run: npm run validate
      - name: Construir el sitio
        run: npm run build
      - name: Pruebas (función de formularios y páginas generadas)
        run: npm test
      - name: Empaquetar la función como lo hace Cloudflare Pages
        run: npx wrangler pages functions build --outdir /tmp/functions-build
      - name: README al día con los datos
        run: npm run readme:check

repository.name: easyeda-agent
repository.readme:
easyeda-agent

让 AI 直接操作嘉立创 EDA 专业版：读数据手册、画原理图、布局 PCB、整理丝印并完成检查。

GitHub · 立创插件市场 · 快速开始 · CLI Status · English

![easyeda-agent workflow](docs/assets/easyeda-agent-workflow.svg) `easyeda-agent` 是 EasyEDA Pro（嘉立创 EDA 专业版）的 AI 自动化层。你可以直接描述想做的 电路或要修的问题，Agent 会读取真实工程数据，通过官方 `eda.*` API 完成操作，并在写入前后 检查器件身份、引脚网络、几何、DRC 和保存状态。 ## 它能做什么 | 使用场景 | 能力 | |---|---| | **拿 PDF / 尺寸图建库** | 读取型号、引脚和封装证据，创建 Symbol、Footprint、Device 和可选 3D Model；校验来源、焊盘依据和 pin↔pad 映射。[实战：AS07 私有库与框外丝印](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/README.md) | | **从需求做到一块板** | 从自然语言需求完成选型、原理图、分区布局、PCB、板框、叠层、布线、铺铜、丝印、DRC 和制造检查 | | **原理图器件标准化** | 用 LCSC C 号或准确型号替换非标准器件，保留位号、位置和 PCB 同步身份；报告引脚差异并指导重新接线 | | **原理图整理与修复** | 读取完整连接图，检查悬空、短路、跨页网名、NC、位号和模块归属，重新排版并回读验证 | | **PCB 布局与布线** | 模块感知自动布局、板框贴合、规则感知短线布线、过孔、铺铜、4 层电源平面、天线 keepout | | **丝印调整** | 自动避开焊盘、器件体、禁区、板框和其他标签；添加板注、接口名、LED 极性及 SVG Logo | | **复用成熟电路** | 从内置电路块库复用 CH340、ESP32 自动下载、按键、USB Hub、降压等拓扑，放件、连线并对账 | | **检查与交付** | 原理图连接与几何检查、PCB DRC/DFM、BOM、网表、制造文件、截图、审计日志和显式保存 | 当前可用范围与检查进度见 [CLI Status](docs/cli-STATUS.md)，完整能力见 [功能清单](docs/FEATURES.md)，命令索引见 [原理图 CLI](docs/cli/schematic.md) 和 [PCB CLI](docs/cli/pcb.md)。 ## 直接这样告诉 Agent 安装完成后，不需要先学习 CLI。把需求和必要的文件交给支持 Skill 的 Agent，并明确使用 `easyeda-agent`。 ### 用 PDF 创建器件库 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent，根据附件 ABC123.pdf 为完整型号 ABC123-QFN 建库。 先检查 EasyEDA 和 LCSC 库是否已有完全匹配的器件；没有再通读整份数据手册，核对订购 后缀、引脚表、封装尺寸图和推荐焊盘。自动创建 Symbol、Footprint 和 Device，保留证据页码， 先运行离线规格校验，再写入个人库。完成后回读 pin↔pad 映射并放置一个实例检查 Pin-1。 只有手册确实存在多个无法消歧的封装或缺少关键尺寸时再问我。 ``` 这个流程使用 `easyeda lib device validate --spec …` 在打开或修改 EasyEDA 前检查数据手册 证据、几何和引脚映射，再由 `lib device build` 创建完整资产。规格契约见 [数据手册驱动的自动建库](.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/references/library-authoring.md)。 ### 做一块 ESP32 最小系统板 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent，在项目 ceshi 中完成一块 ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 最小系统板： 5V 端子输入，降压到 3V3，CH340 USB 下载，BOOT/RESET 按键，一颗 GPIO 控制的 LED， 四角 M3 固定孔。做 4 层板，GND 内电层，模组天线区域所有层 keepout。 请自行选型并核对数据手册，从原理图、布局、布线、铺铜、丝印一直做到 DRC 和保存完成。 ``` 完整实战与真实截图见 [一份需求文档 → ESP32-S3 四层板](docs/showcase-esp32-mini.md)。 ### 调整当前 PCB 的丝印 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 检查当前 PCB 的全部位号和自由丝印。把压焊盘、超板框、重叠、 朝向不一致和底层未镜像的问题整理好；保留 LED 正负极、接口名称和必要板注。 完成后运行 pcb check 和官方 DRC，导出一张复核图并保存。 ``` ### 标准化原理图器件 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 扫描当前原理图，把无准确料号、非标准符号或封装不一致的器件列出来。 优先匹配标准器件库和准确 LCSC C 号，核对型号、封装及引脚后再替换。 替换时保留位号、位置和 uniqueId；如果 pinDiff 非空，修复接线并重新运行 sch check、 bridge-check 和官方 DRC。最后输出替换清单和仍无法确定的器件。 ``` ### 检查并修复已有工程 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 全面检查当前原理图和 PCB。先读取真实器件、引脚、网络、板框、叠层和 DRC 规则，再修复可以确定的问题。不要凭截图猜连接；所有修改完成后回读对账、运行连接/几何/DRC 检查、 保存，并把仍需人工决策的问题单独列出。 ``` ## 效果展示 ### 从模块尺寸图到个人私有库 **需求：** 按用户提供的 AS07-M1101D-SMA 尺寸与引脚图创建个人库，原理图保持双排引脚的 左右顺序；封装标注引脚名和型号，丝印全部放在模块覆盖区域外，安装后仍可查看，并收紧、对齐。 **结果：** 已创建并保存 Symbol、Footprint 和 Device，核对 8 个引脚与 8 个通孔焊盘映射； 修正符号边框闭合和引脚方向。封装左侧用两列脚号＋名称，列间距约 0.5 mm，靠框一列距框 约 0.6 mm；型号居中放在框外上方，实际文字包围盒回读无重叠。 最终按用户要求使用普通引脚线和未定义类型，1 脚使用独立圆形标记；保留用户清理 NC 后的状态。 ![AS07 原理图符号：与用户引脚图一致的左右顺序](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/symbol.png) 这次输入是用户尺寸图，不是完整原厂 PDF；焊盘与部分偏移采用明确假设计算。 尚未验证实物装配、放置实例和 PCB DRC，不作为生产就绪证明。 [查看原始需求图、封装预览、规格与回读结果](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/README.md)。 ### 嘉立创 PCB 初级考试第十八期：AT32F415 Layout 当前参数化 Layout 基线包含 69 个器件、15 个功能区和 90 × 50 mm 圆角板框，用于验证 “样例关系 → 算法候选 → AI 选择 → typed 写入 → 回读”的布局方法。该图展示布局阶段结果， 不代表整板布线或生产检查已经完成。

标准考试来源：**嘉立创 PCB 初级考试题第十八期**。执行步骤、参数和验证边界见 [260919 AT32F415 考试执行指导](docs/260919-exam-execution-guide.md)。 ### ESP32-S3 四层板（历史案例） Agent 完成原理图到 PCB 的完整流程，包括模块布局、圆角板框、4 层电源结构、天线净空、 规则感知布线、铺铜和丝印整理。 ![AI 在 EasyEDA 中完成 PCB 布局、板框和铺铜](docs/assets/demo-pcb-layout.gif) | 板框贴合 | 丝印避让 | |---|---| | → | → 整理结果见成品板 | ### 数据驱动的原理图组合 Agent 先在本地连接数据中核对器件、引脚和网络，再计算模块内部布局并写回 EasyEDA；粉色虚线框 表示独立功能区，Apply 后逐脚回读，而不是仅凭截图判断成功。 ![门禁控制板的电源与 RF 主控原理图](docs/images/access-control-power-rf.png) ![原理图实际 Apply 过程](docs/assets/access-control-sch-apply.gif) ## 安装与开始使用 easyeda-agent 由三部分组成：`easyeda` CLI/daemon、运行在 EasyEDA 内的 **EDA Agent Connector**，以及安装在 AI 客户端中的 `easyeda-agent` Skill。 ### 1. 安装 CLI 和 Skill macOS / Linux： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/main/install.sh | bash ``` 原生 Windows（Windows PowerShell 5.1 或 PowerShell 7）： ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` 两个脚本行为一致：先取 `checksums.txt`，全部资产校验 SHA-256、核对 CLI `--version` 与 Skill `metadata.version` 之后才替换已安装文件；环境变量 `EASYEDA_VERSION`、 `EASYEDA_INSTALL_DIR`、`EASYEDA_INSTALL_SKILLS`、`EASYEDA_SKILL_PRESERVE`、 `EASYEDA_GITHUB_PROXY` 同样生效。安装器会识别 Codex、Codex Desktop 和 Claude Code， 并打印连接器下载地址。 install.ps1 默认装到 `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`，不会自作主张改 PATH：目录不在用户 PATH 上时只打印添加命令，需要自动添加用 `-AddToPath`（下载成文件运行）或 `$env:EASYEDA_ADD_TO_PATH=1`（管道运行）；机器级 PATH 始终不动。手工安装步骤见 [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md)。 ### 2. 安装连接器 从 [立创插件市场](https://jlc-ext.com/item/zhoushoujian/easyeda-agent-connector) 安装，或从 [最新 GitHub Release](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/releases/latest) 下载 `easyeda-agent-connector.eext` 后在 EasyEDA Pro 的扩展管理器中导入。 ### 3. 打开工程并检查 打开目标 EasyEDA 工程，并启用 **设置 → 允许外部交互**，然后运行： ```bash easyeda health ``` 它逐项列出 daemon、连接器、版本、EasyEDA 宿主、工程与标签页是否就绪，未就绪项直接给出下一步。 daemon 不用手动常驻：任何 `easyeda` 命令发现它没在运行时会自动在后台启动（日志在 `~/.easyeda-agent/daemon.log`；`EASYEDA_NO_AUTOSTART=1` 关闭）。需要安装对账时再运行 `easyeda update --check --exit-code`。 项目主线要求 **EasyEDA Pro V4**，推荐升级到已验证的 **V4.1.60 或更新 V4**。 `easyeda health` 会在 `hostCompatibility` 中单独报告宿主产品版本；V3 环境应先升级再做现场写入。 V4 适配进度和边界见 [V4 开发台账](docs/v4-development.md)。 版本差异会作为诊断输出，不作为设计动作的许可。Connector 若缺少当前动作或协议不兼容， 按诊断升级对应组件；Skill 内容更新后让客户端重新加载它。 更详细的安装、升级、代理和排障步骤见 [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md)。 ## 为什么它适合 Agent 直接把任意 JavaScript 丢进编辑器很难审查，也难确认部分失败。easyeda-agent 把常用能力封装成 有明确输入输出的 typed actions，并在工作流中加入： - 写入前检查目标工程、页面、器件身份和源数据； - 写入后回读引脚、网络、几何和对象绑定； - 原理图 `layout-lint → check → bridge-check → DRC` 分项报告事实与差异； - PCB 使用真实 DRC 规则完成布局、布线、铺铜和制造检查； - 对部分成功、超时和无法确认的结果停止盲目重试； - 自动保存作为安全网，关键节点仍显式保存。 ```text AI Agent / Skill │ ▼ easyeda CLI + local daemon │ typed actions / audit / artifacts ▼ EDA Agent Connector (.eext) │ official eda.* API ▼ EasyEDA Pro project ``` 架构与协议细节见 [架构说明](docs/architecture.md) 和 [协议说明](docs/protocol.md)。 ## 能力边界 - 稠密板的完整迷宫自动布线需要外部 Freerouting；内置路由器适合短线和清晰局部连接。 - EasyEDA 扩展 API 不提供编程式 undo，项目通过源数据、写前守卫、回读和失败回滚降低风险。 - 受控阻抗所需的介质厚度、Er 和铜厚无法从当前 `eda.*` API 完整读取，不能自动声称阻抗合格。 - PDF 自动建库仍以具体型号和原厂证据为准；扫描模糊、封装后缀不明或缺少焊盘依据时会暂停询问。 当前能力与边界见 [功能清单](docs/FEATURES.md) 和 [CLI 索引](docs/cli/README.md)。 过往调研和实测结果集中在 [历史证据索引](docs/reviews/README.md)。 ## 开发与贡献 - PCB 算法贡献：[四个公共 Go 包、数学问题与可认领任务](docs/pcb-solver-community-design.md)；`make pcb-solver-test` 可离线运行，无需 EDA。 - 文档导航与信息归属：[docs/README.md](docs/README.md) - 跨项目查询、维护 Skill 和多客户端兼容：[Agent 协作设计](docs/agent-collaboration.md) - 开发环境：[docs/dev-environment.md](docs/dev-environment.md) - 电路块贡献：[standard-blocks-contributing.md](.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/references/standard-blocks-contributing.md) - Skill 入口：[.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/SKILL.md) - 仓库结构与开发约定：[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) 感谢嘉立创 EDA 专业版开放扩展接口，也感谢 [@jlceda/pro-api-types](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jlceda/pro-api-types)、 [Freerouting](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting) 及 [EasyEDA 官方开源扩展](https://github.com/easyeda) 提供的基础与参考。 ## 许可证 [MIT](LICENSE)。`extension/src/beautify/` 中移植自 [Easy_EDA_PCB_Beautify](https://github.com/m-RNA/Easy_EDA_PCB_Beautify) 的文件沿用 Apache-2.0，详见 [NOTICE](NOTICE)。 ## Star History 感谢每一颗 star。 [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent&type=Date)](https://www.star-history.com/#zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent&Date)

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, dev]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  pcb-solvers:
    name: PCB solver packages (offline)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - name: Verify public solver packages and file cases
        run: make pcb-solver-test

  test:
    name: CLI, connector and Skill
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: |
            package-lock.json
            extension/package-lock.json
            mcp/package-lock.json
      - name: Test and build CLI
        run: |
          make test
          make mcp-test
      - name: Validate Skill, Agent collaboration and release helpers
        run: |
          make lint-test
          make modules-audit
          make release-script-test
          make agent-check
          make skill-check
          npx --yes skills-ref@latest validate .agents/skills/easyeda-agent
      - name: Test and build connector
        run: |
          npm --prefix extension ci --ignore-scripts
          npm --prefix extension run typecheck
          npm --prefix extension test
          npm --prefix extension run build

  native-release-smoke:
    name: Native install surface (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json
      - name: Verify DSH bundle distribution, file paths and native MCP launch
        run: |
          npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run test:dsh
      - name: Verify native download, version check and temporary replacement
        run: go test ./internal/selfupdate -run '^TestNativeDownloadedBinaryVerificationAndReplacement$' -count=1 -v
      - name: Verify component patch files and legacy PowerShell argument passing
        run: go test ./internal/app -run '^TestModifyPatch' -count=1 -v
      - name: Build and smoke a native CLI outside the checkout
        shell: bash
        run: |
          smoke_version="v$(python -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("extension/extension.json"))["version"])')"
          # Between releases extension.json carries a -dev.N version, which is not a
          # publishable tag. Tell the smoke test which form to expect, the same way
          # the Makefile's local-build target does for release-check.py.
          local_dev=""
          case "$smoke_version" in *-dev.*) local_dev="--local-dev" ;; esac
          go build -ldflags "-X github.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/internal/version.Version=$smoke_version" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/easyeda-smoke.exe" ./cmd/easyeda
          python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p test_release_smoke.py
          python scripts/release-smoke.py --version "$smoke_version" $local_dev --binary "$RUNNER_TEMP/easyeda-smoke.exe" --skill-dir .agents/skills/easyeda-agent

sampled_files.README.md:
easyeda-agent

让 AI 直接操作嘉立创 EDA 专业版：读数据手册、画原理图、布局 PCB、整理丝印并完成检查。

GitHub · 立创插件市场 · 快速开始 · CLI Status · English

![easyeda-agent workflow](docs/assets/easyeda-agent-workflow.svg) `easyeda-agent` 是 EasyEDA Pro（嘉立创 EDA 专业版）的 AI 自动化层。你可以直接描述想做的 电路或要修的问题，Agent 会读取真实工程数据，通过官方 `eda.*` API 完成操作，并在写入前后 检查器件身份、引脚网络、几何、DRC 和保存状态。 ## 它能做什么 | 使用场景 | 能力 | |---|---| | **拿 PDF / 尺寸图建库** | 读取型号、引脚和封装证据，创建 Symbol、Footprint、Device 和可选 3D Model；校验来源、焊盘依据和 pin↔pad 映射。[实战：AS07 私有库与框外丝印](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/README.md) | | **从需求做到一块板** | 从自然语言需求完成选型、原理图、分区布局、PCB、板框、叠层、布线、铺铜、丝印、DRC 和制造检查 | | **原理图器件标准化** | 用 LCSC C 号或准确型号替换非标准器件，保留位号、位置和 PCB 同步身份；报告引脚差异并指导重新接线 | | **原理图整理与修复** | 读取完整连接图，检查悬空、短路、跨页网名、NC、位号和模块归属，重新排版并回读验证 | | **PCB 布局与布线** | 模块感知自动布局、板框贴合、规则感知短线布线、过孔、铺铜、4 层电源平面、天线 keepout | | **丝印调整** | 自动避开焊盘、器件体、禁区、板框和其他标签；添加板注、接口名、LED 极性及 SVG Logo | | **复用成熟电路** | 从内置电路块库复用 CH340、ESP32 自动下载、按键、USB Hub、降压等拓扑，放件、连线并对账 | | **检查与交付** | 原理图连接与几何检查、PCB DRC/DFM、BOM、网表、制造文件、截图、审计日志和显式保存 | 当前可用范围与检查进度见 [CLI Status](docs/cli-STATUS.md)，完整能力见 [功能清单](docs/FEATURES.md)，命令索引见 [原理图 CLI](docs/cli/schematic.md) 和 [PCB CLI](docs/cli/pcb.md)。 ## 直接这样告诉 Agent 安装完成后，不需要先学习 CLI。把需求和必要的文件交给支持 Skill 的 Agent，并明确使用 `easyeda-agent`。 ### 用 PDF 创建器件库 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent，根据附件 ABC123.pdf 为完整型号 ABC123-QFN 建库。 先检查 EasyEDA 和 LCSC 库是否已有完全匹配的器件；没有再通读整份数据手册，核对订购 后缀、引脚表、封装尺寸图和推荐焊盘。自动创建 Symbol、Footprint 和 Device，保留证据页码， 先运行离线规格校验，再写入个人库。完成后回读 pin↔pad 映射并放置一个实例检查 Pin-1。 只有手册确实存在多个无法消歧的封装或缺少关键尺寸时再问我。 ``` 这个流程使用 `easyeda lib device validate --spec …` 在打开或修改 EasyEDA 前检查数据手册 证据、几何和引脚映射，再由 `lib device build` 创建完整资产。规格契约见 [数据手册驱动的自动建库](.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/references/library-authoring.md)。 ### 做一块 ESP32 最小系统板 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent，在项目 ceshi 中完成一块 ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 最小系统板： 5V 端子输入，降压到 3V3，CH340 USB 下载，BOOT/RESET 按键，一颗 GPIO 控制的 LED， 四角 M3 固定孔。做 4 层板，GND 内电层，模组天线区域所有层 keepout。 请自行选型并核对数据手册，从原理图、布局、布线、铺铜、丝印一直做到 DRC 和保存完成。 ``` 完整实战与真实截图见 [一份需求文档 → ESP32-S3 四层板](docs/showcase-esp32-mini.md)。 ### 调整当前 PCB 的丝印 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 检查当前 PCB 的全部位号和自由丝印。把压焊盘、超板框、重叠、 朝向不一致和底层未镜像的问题整理好；保留 LED 正负极、接口名称和必要板注。 完成后运行 pcb check 和官方 DRC，导出一张复核图并保存。 ``` ### 标准化原理图器件 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 扫描当前原理图，把无准确料号、非标准符号或封装不一致的器件列出来。 优先匹配标准器件库和准确 LCSC C 号，核对型号、封装及引脚后再替换。 替换时保留位号、位置和 uniqueId；如果 pinDiff 非空，修复接线并重新运行 sch check、 bridge-check 和官方 DRC。最后输出替换清单和仍无法确定的器件。 ``` ### 检查并修复已有工程 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 全面检查当前原理图和 PCB。先读取真实器件、引脚、网络、板框、叠层和 DRC 规则，再修复可以确定的问题。不要凭截图猜连接；所有修改完成后回读对账、运行连接/几何/DRC 检查、 保存，并把仍需人工决策的问题单独列出。 ``` ## 效果展示 ### 从模块尺寸图到个人私有库 **需求：** 按用户提供的 AS07-M1101D-SMA 尺寸与引脚图创建个人库，原理图保持双排引脚的 左右顺序；封装标注引脚名和型号，丝印全部放在模块覆盖区域外，安装后仍可查看，并收紧、对齐。 **结果：** 已创建并保存 Symbol、Footprint 和 Device，核对 8 个引脚与 8 个通孔焊盘映射； 修正符号边框闭合和引脚方向。封装左侧用两列脚号＋名称，列间距约 0.5 mm，靠框一列距框 约 0.6 mm；型号居中放在框外上方，实际文字包围盒回读无重叠。 最终按用户要求使用普通引脚线和未定义类型，1 脚使用独立圆形标记；保留用户清理 NC 后的状态。 ![AS07 原理图符号：与用户引脚图一致的左右顺序](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/symbol.png) 这次输入是用户尺寸图，不是完整原厂 PDF；焊盘与部分偏移采用明确假设计算。 尚未验证实物装配、放置实例和 PCB DRC，不作为生产就绪证明。 [查看原始需求图、封装预览、规格与回读结果](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/README.md)。 ### 嘉立创 PCB 初级考试第十八期：AT32F415 Layout 当前参数化 Layout 基线包含 69 个器件、15 个功能区和 90 × 50 mm 圆角板框，用于验证 “样例关系 → 算法候选 → AI 选择 → typed 写入 → 回读”的布局方法。该图展示布局阶段结果， 不代表整板布线或生产检查已经完成。

标准考试来源：**嘉立创 PCB 初级考试题第十八期**。执行步骤、参数和验证边界见 [260919 AT32F415 考试执行指导](docs/260919-exam-execution-guide.md)。 ### ESP32-S3 四层板（历史案例） Agent 完成原理图到 PCB 的完整流程，包括模块布局、圆角板框、4 层电源结构、天线净空、 规则感知布线、铺铜和丝印整理。 ![AI 在 EasyEDA 中完成 PCB 布局、板框和铺铜](docs/assets/demo-pcb-layout.gif) | 板框贴合 | 丝印避让 | |---|---| | → | → 整理结果见成品板 | ### 数据驱动的原理图组合 Agent 先在本地连接数据中核对器件、引脚和网络，再计算模块内部布局并写回 EasyEDA；粉色虚线框 表示独立功能区，Apply 后逐脚回读，而不是仅凭截图判断成功。 ![门禁控制板的电源与 RF 主控原理图](docs/images/access-control-power-rf.png) ![原理图实际 Apply 过程](docs/assets/access-control-sch-apply.gif) ## 安装与开始使用 easyeda-agent 由三部分组成：`easyeda` CLI/daemon、运行在 EasyEDA 内的 **EDA Agent Connector**，以及安装在 AI 客户端中的 `easyeda-agent` Skill。 ### 1. 安装 CLI 和 Skill macOS / Linux： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/main/install.sh | bash ``` 原生 Windows（Windows PowerShell 5.1 或 PowerShell 7）： ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` 两个脚本行为一致：先取 `checksums.txt`，全部资产校验 SHA-256、核对 CLI `--version` 与 Skill `metadata.version` 之后才替换已安装文件；环境变量 `EASYEDA_VERSION`、 `EASYEDA_INSTALL_DIR`、`EASYEDA_INSTALL_SKILLS`、`EASYEDA_SKILL_PRESERVE`、 `EASYEDA_GITHUB_PROXY` 同样生效。安装器会识别 Codex、Codex Desktop 和 Claude Code， 并打印连接器下载地址。 install.ps1 默认装到 `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`，不会自作主张改 PATH：目录不在用户 PATH 上时只打印添加命令，需要自动添加用 `-AddToPath`（下载成文件运行）或 `$env:EASYEDA_ADD_TO_PATH=1`（管道运行）；机器级 PATH 始终不动。手工安装步骤见 [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md)。 ### 2. 安装连接器 从 [立创插件市场](https://jlc-ext.com/item/zhoushoujian/easyeda-agent-connector) 安装，或从 [最新 GitHub Release](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/releases/latest) 下载 `easyeda-agent-connector.eext` 后在 EasyEDA Pro 的扩展管理器中导入。 ### 3. 打开工程并检查 打开目标 EasyEDA 工程，并启用 **设置 → 允许外部交互**，然后运行： ```bash easyeda health ``` 它逐项列出 daemon、连接器、版本、EasyEDA 宿主、工程与标签页是否就绪，未就绪项直接给出下一步。 daemon 不用手动常驻：任何 `easyeda` 命令发现它没在运行时会自动在后台启动（日志在 `~/.easyeda-agent/daemon.log`；`EASYEDA_NO_AUTOSTART=1` 关闭）。需要安装对账时再运行 `easyeda update --check --exit-code`。 项目主线要求 **EasyEDA Pro V4**，推荐升级到已验证的 **V4.1.60 或更新 V4**。 `easyeda health` 会在 `hostCompatibility` 中单独报告宿主产品版本；V3 环境应先升级再做现场写入。 V4 适配进度和边界见 [V4 开发台账](docs/v4-development.md)。 版本差异会作为诊断输出，不作为设计动作的许可。Connector 若缺少当前动作或协议不兼容， 按诊断升级对应组件；Skill 内容更新后让客户端重新加载它。 更详细的安装、升级、代理和排障步骤见 [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md)。 ## 为什么它适合 Agent 直接把任意 JavaScript 丢进编辑器很难审查，也难确认部分失败。easyeda-agent 把常用能力封装成 有明确输入输出的 typed actions，并在工作流中加入： - 写入前检查目标工程、页面、器件身份和源数据； - 写入后回读引脚、网络、几何和对象绑定； - 原理图 `layout-lint → check → bridge-check → DRC` 分项报告事实与差异； - PCB 使用真实 DRC 规则完成布局、布线、铺铜和制造检查； - 对部分成功、超时和无法确认的结果停止盲目重试； - 自动保存作为安全网，关键节点仍显式保存。 ```text AI Agent / Skill │ ▼ easyeda CLI + local daemon │ typed actions / audit / artifacts ▼ EDA Agent Connector (.eext) │ official eda.* API ▼ EasyEDA Pro project ``` 架构与协议细节见 [架构说明](docs/architecture.md) 和 [协议说明](docs/protocol.md)。 ## 能力边界 - 稠密板的完整迷宫自动布线需要外部 Freerouting；内置路由器适合短线和清晰局部连接。 - EasyEDA 扩展 API 不提供编程式 undo，项目通过源数据、写前守卫、回读和失败回滚降低风险。 - 受控阻抗所需的介质厚度、Er 和铜厚无法从当前 `eda.*` API 完整读取，不能自动声称阻抗合格。 - PDF 自动建库仍以具体型号和原厂证据为准；扫描模糊、封装后缀不明或缺少焊盘依据时会暂停询问。 当前能力与边界见 [功能清单](docs/FEATURES.md) 和 [CLI 索引](docs/cli/README.md)。 过往调研和实测结果集中在 [历史证据索引](docs/reviews/README.md)。 ##
